speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator voice)
question:
The prathamo vimarśa gave the categories of the *known* (prameya). Now the dvitīyo
vimarśa examines the *knowers* (pramātṛ) themselves — for the recognition of the Lord in the self is
the heart of the whole śāstra, and to recognize him we must understand the various knowers: the bound
(paśu) in its grades, the pure ones, and the Lord (pati). Central here are the *malas* (the stains that
bind): āṇava (the stain of finitude), māyīya (the stain of māyā, objectivity), and kārma (the stain of
action). Kārikās 1–11 lay out the knower-states, their presiding deities, and the stains.
premises:
"Bowing to the nectar-bodied, the full-param-essence of the three powers, who wields the trident,
cutting the three nooses (pāśatraya) in diseases and the rest…" Having established the tattva-mass as
the known, now the knower-tattva is examined at length (20 verses): one on the Brahmādi-three (k1);
two on the division of the to-be-abandoned/to-be-adopted knowers; seven on the stain's form and the
knower-variety it makes (k2–8); two on the entry (samāveśa); five on the states (suṣupta etc.); three
on their abandon/adopt division.

> There, in the knower-mere-ness-standing, the Rudra the superior-deity; in the distinct-known-spread,
> the Brahmā and Viṣṇu are established.

In the state where the knower is pure, with the known withdrawn (upasaṃhṛta-prameya), the presider is
the Rudra — the param-Śiva, as the Lord, who by his presiding brings his worshippers to that state. In
the māyā-word, the prāṇāpāna-form, he is the third-eyed (unmīlita-tṛtīyanetra). In the spread of the
*distinct* known, the presider is Brahmā (in the production of the spread) and Viṣṇu (in the flowing
continuation of it). These two, making the "this" primary (as manifestation) and the "I" (the knower-
essence) subordinate, are not third-eyed — the deity (daivata) is the presiding-form, and the
adhidaivata is the deity-as-superior. The objection "how do the Brahmādi-forms shine with the
un-purified form of the Lord?" — answered: as the quality of the intellect (buddhiguṇa), not as the
pure consciousness-mere; hence their form is the aiśvarya (the lordship, the freedom as action-power,
the knowledge). The duality is explained.
> This knower, the māyā-blind, the saṃsāra-one, the action-bound —

[The bound knower (paśu) is blind by māyā, a wanderer in saṃsāra, bound by action (karma). This is
the māyīya knower.]

> In the own-member-form beings, the knower is said [to be] the Lord (pati). — 3
> The freedom-loss of the awareness; the freedom-own-even the un-awareness-ness. — 4

[The pati is the knower whose own-members (the beings) are his; the bound one suffers the
freedom-loss of the awareness (svātantryahāni) and the un-awareness of his own freedom — the
āṇava/māyīya binding.]
> The distinct-known-manifestation, here alone, the māyā-named, the birth-enjoyment-giving —

[Māyā is the manifestation of the distinct known (the objectivity), which gives birth and enjoyment;
it is the māyīya stain.]

> In the pure-awareness-own-ness even, of-whom-not-the-highest-agent-ness — 6
> In the awareness-and-the-rest-marker-unity-even, of-them-the-mutual-distinct-ness — 7
> The emptiness-and-the-rest-un-awareness-form-ones-though, the agents, the dissolution-un-caliber-ones — 8

[The pure knowers (the vidyeśvara group) who lack the highest agency; the mutual distinct-ness even in
the unity of the awareness-marker; and the pralayākala (the "dissolution-un-caliber" — those who have
only the āṇava stain, absorbed in the dissolution), whose form is the emptiness-and-the-rest
un-awareness.]

> Of the awareness-ones-even agent-ness-possessing, in the action-stain-ness — 9
> Of the gods-and-the-rest, and of all the becoming-ones, the three-fold stain — 10

[Even the aware agents are in the kārma stain; and all the becoming ones (gods, men, etc.) have the
three-fold stain: āṇava, māyīya, kārma.]
> The time-raised (kalā-udbalita), this, the consciousness-essence, the agent-ness-made —

[The kalā (the limited agency) raises the consciousness-essence as the agent-ness; the last of the
kañcukas binding the self to limited agency.]
inference:
Decision for L2
Proceed. The argument is understood: the knower-tattva is examined — the presiding deities (Rudra,
Brahmā, Viṣṇu) of the knower-states; the bound knower blind by māyā and bound by action; the pati (the
Lord of the own-members); the freedom-loss; māyā as the distinct-known-manifestation; the grades of the
pure and dissolved knowers; the three-fold stain (āṇava, māyīya, kārma); and the kalā-raised
consciousness-essence. The malas are the binding, and their cutting is the release.
uncertainties: The exact enumeration of the vidyeśvara/pralayākala/vijñānākala grades (k6–8) — the text is dense;
The "unmīlita-tṛtīyanetra" (the opened third eye) of the Rudra in the māyā-word — the symbol is

speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator voice)
question:
Having examined the knowers and the stains, Abhinavagupta now examines the *states*
(avasthā) of the bound knower — jāgrat (waking), svapna (dream), suṣupta (deep sleep), and turya (the
fourth) — and the vital breaths (prāṇādi) that sustain them. The point: these states are the stages in
which the bound soul lives, and understanding them — which are to be adopted (upādeya) and which
abandoned (heya) — is essential to the recognition. The pure fourth state is the goal; the other three
are the round of the bound.
premises: > The primary-ness of the agent-ness, and of the awareness, and of the consciousness-self —

[The knower's essence: agency (kartṛtā), awareness (bodha), and the consciousness-self (cidātman) are
primary. This frames the whole — the knower is fundamentally the free conscious agent.]
> In the emptiness, the intellect-and-the-rest-absence-own, the I-ness, the agent-ness-word —

[In the state of the void (śūnya), where the intellect and the rest are absent, the "I-ness" and the
"agent-ness" are only words — the pralayākala, dissolved in the void, has the mere trace of the
"I".]
> The inner operation of the senses, the breath-and-the-rest-stimulating, the thought —

[The prāṇa (the vital breath) is the inner operation that stimulates the senses; it is the life of the
bound knower, the link between the self and the senses.]

> In the that-much-standing, the said, the sleep-like-the-dissolution-equal — with the known, and
> without-the-known, with-the-māyā-stain, and-without —

In the mere void (śūnyamātra) — the pure void — when the standing is the I-ness-rest (ahantāviśrānti),
and when [it is] in the prāṇa, then the consciousness is put to sleep by the māyā (which makes the
stain descend), not even awakened by kalā and vidyā. This is the suṣupta (deep sleep): the
pravṛtti-cause-form appearance, and the karma (as the action-form) whose essence is the
reflexive-awareness. Deep sleep is like dissolution (pralaya) — but in dissolution there is the long
decay of the body; here, in sleep, there is no such action and no long time. Its sub-kinds: sleep
(by fatigue), fainting (by shock/dhātu-disease), intoxication/madness (by wine, etc.), samādhi (by
the freedom-raised effort). The first half is "with the known" (savedya, the vidyākalā grade, with the
māyā-stain), the second "without the known" (apavedya, without the māyā-stain, the pralayākala).

> In the mind-mere-path even, with the sense-object-ness, from the delusion — the clear-manifestation
> creation of the beings, the dream-word, the thought.

In the dream, the sense-organs (the eyes and the rest) are fixed, yet one sees the beloved, and the
cognition "I see her, I draw her with my hand" is a clear manifestation whose primary [source] is the
momentary Lord-creation. Only the mind is active, relying on the prior creation; but in the
sense-object-part, [the dream] shares the common [world]; the stability and the rest of the
appearance, joined, continue the reflexive-awareness — and in the waking state, this is refuted, so the
dream is of the delusion-form. The dream is the mind's own creation, a clear-appearance making.

> With-the-all-sense-object-ness, which-though-with-the-external-ness-firm — the creation, the
> common, of-all-the-knowers, that is the waking.

The waking state is the *common* creation (sādhāraṇī sṛṣṭi), firm and external, shared by all the
knowers. The waking knower is he who, by the exhaustion of the delusion-causing sleep, "wakes" —
so the waking is the knower-state. The five states (waking, dream, deep sleep, and the two grades) are
the knower-ness made by the difference of the known, as taught in the āgamas; and even in the waking
the dream-form is found (the mutual entry of the states).

> The removable, the three, this, of the breath-and-the-rest, from the primary-ness, in the
> agent-ness-quality — from its decrease-increase-mostly-joined-suffering-pleasure —

The three states (waking, dream, deep sleep) are to be abandoned (heya) by the seeker of liberation,
since the prāṇa and the rest (the vital breaths) are primary in the agent-ness, and the decrease/
increase of pleasure and pain is their quality. In the agent-ness, where the prāṇa is not made primary,
its freedom-share, with the pleasure/pain-objects and the gaining/abandoning-efforts, makes the seeker
regard the three states as to-be-abandoned.

> The breath-out-breath-made, the breath, individually in-the-sleep-waking-two — 19
> The middle-upper-going, the udāna-named, the-fourth-going, the-fire-made — 20

[The prāṇa (the in-breath) and the apāna (the out-breath) run through the waking and the sleep; the
udāna is the middle-upper-going breath; the turya (the fourth) is the going beyond — of the fire-form
(hutabhuṅmaya). The prāṇas are the life-winds that sustain the states; the turya is the fourth state,
beyond the three, which is the goal.]
the close of the āgamādhikāra dvitīyo vimarśa and the āgamādhikāra.
inference:
Decision for L2
Proceed. The argument is understood: the knower is fundamentally the free conscious agent (k12); the
bound states are the round of waking, dream, and deep sleep (k15–17) — deep sleep like dissolution
(with/without the māyā-stain), dream the mind's clear creation, waking the common firm creation — all
three to be abandoned (k18) for the sake of the fourth, the turya, the pure state; and the vital
breaths (k19–20) sustain these states, the turya being the fire-form that goes beyond. The recognition
leads the bound knower from the three to the fourth.
uncertainties: The exact prāṇa enumeration (prāṇa, apāna, udāna, samāna, vyāna) — kārikās 19–20 give the
The savedya/apavedya grades of suṣupta (vidyākalā vs. pralayākala) — the two grades with/without

speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator voice)
question:
This is the fourth and final adhikāra of the IPVV — the tattvasaṅgrahādhikāra, the
"collection of the essence of the categories." Having established the self-manifest ātmatattva (the
maheśvara-form, the knowledge-action power) at length, in three adhikāras, Abhinavagupta now collects
the whole into a brief summary (15 verses) for the student's meditation. One verse gives the
pāramārthika svarūpa; nine give the bond (bandha) in the direction of the knower/known; five give the
liberation (mokṣa) which is the recognition (pratyabhijñā). Kārikās 1–8 are the opening: the own-self
as the Lord, the bound grasper, the many person, and the guṇas.
premises:
"I bow to him, the nectar-Lord, who, in his un-surpassed own abode, makes the drop-made nectar-juice
known, the fully-full-making…" The plan: 15 verses — one on the pāramārthika svarūpa (k1), nine on the
bond in the knower/known direction (k2–10), five on the recognition-liberation (k11–15).

> The own-self alone of all beings, the one alone, the maheśvara — the world-form, "I this," the
> un-broken-re-recollection-augmented.

The sūtra is introduced after the spread declaration (vitatābhidhāna). The non-repetition: those not
wanting the spread are graced by the epitome; those wanting the middle are served. (Cites the muni's
rule "the desired, in the world, of the wise, is the summary-and-detail-bearing.") The "beings" word
carries the burden: "this whole is the person alone." So the teaching is: the own-self alone of all
beings is the one Lord, the world-form, whose re-recollection "I-this" is un-broken. (As the
Śivadṛṣṭi: "all beings are Śiva; the self of all beings is Śiva" — not that Śiva-seeing is a mere
doctrine, but that the self-flashing dharma in them is Śiva.)

> There, in the own-created this-being-part, with the intellect-and-the-rest grasper-own, the
> I-construction-re-recollection-word is brought, with this, that.

In the own-self, in the mahā-īśvara, in the own-self-mirror, by the freedom, that which is created —
the this-part, preceded by contraction; in its middle, the intellect/breath/body form, known by the
this-ness; of the that-distinct-known, the grasper-ness-fit, with the I-being, the re-recollection
shines. He, thus-form, "I am happy, and the rest," is the grasper, the bound. His liberation is the
recognition.

> He, the own-form-un-cognition-made, the many person, is the thought; there in the creation, the
> action-bliss two, the enjoyment, is the suffering-pleasure-own.

Truly, no one is bound; in truth the one free Śiva is consciousness-natured. But when the contracted
consciousness manifests, then the un-cognition of the own complete form — with the longing for the
full bliss, the to-be-abandoned-appearance, the woven warp-and-woof, the 
breath/void/body-contraction-variety — thence the many person. He is the enjoyer, the bound; the
enjoyment (bhoga) is the action-bliss two (the kriyā-jñāna powers) seen as pleasure and suffering.

> In the own-member-form beings, of the Lord the knowledge and the action, which — with the māyā-third,
> they alone are of the animal the being-ness (sattva), the rajas, the darkness (tamas).

In the Lord, everywhere, the manifestation-and-reflexive-awareness are the knowledge-action powers; the
māyā-power, opening the this-ness in the Sadāśiva-Īśa word, is the covering. In the own-form-un-
cognition, in the beings, the knowledge and action are the pure-alone distinct-ness; with respect to
the animal, the manifestation/un-manifestation are the sattva/rajas/tamas.

> From the distinction-standing, of the power-possessor, the power-ness is not declared; of these
> qualities, the instrument-effect-ness-transforming.

The distinction-dealing is considered: the contracted consciousness-mere-nature is the person; his
natural manifestation is not a power (by the connection with the other). The sattva-and-the-rest,
standing by the distinction, are not power-declarable. The person, from the enjoyer-form, thinks them
distinct; but in truth, even the earth-end ones, being power-form, are not thus.

> The being-bliss-action of the Lord; the that-absence-even, she, of the animal — the two-own, that
> rajas, the suffering, attached, the sattva-tamas-made.

The Lord's being-ness (sattā) is the flashing, the agent-ness; the action-power is the pure
reflexive-awareness; the bliss-power is the rest-form. Of the animal, the being-ness-bliss is the
that-absence (the absence of the full being-bliss), two-own. The sattva (manifestation-pleasure), the
tamas (the covering), and the rajas (the mixed, attached, suffering).

> Who-even, of the non-conventional-this-ness-re-recollection-ground Lord — they, the mixed, and the
> distinct, thus the varied-manifesting.

In the Lord, even the appearances, mixed and distinct, are the innate (non-conventional)
this-ness-re-recollection, the varied manifestation; in the Īśvara-state, the śūnya (the to-be-removed
void) is the Rudra-presided, manifesting as the I-ness-negation.

> They-though, the distinct-manifestation-meanings, the constructed, of the inner-self — with the
> that-that-distinct-designations, in the memory-conjecture-and-the-rest range.

The Īśvara's objects are the pure reflexive-awareness objects, all; but of the animal, they are the
constructed (vikalpyāḥ), the distinct-manifestation, per-being, per-state, with the own-impression-
following designations ("dear-this, enemy-this"); the inner-self (pratyagātman), the body-and-the-rest
contracted, the "I"-being. The śūnya-pramātṛ, the infinite-regress, and its non-fault close the
vimarśa's core.
inference:
Decision for L2
Proceed. The argument is understood: the tattvasaṅgraha collects the whole — the own-self alone of all
beings is the one Lord (k1); the bound grasper in the own-created this-part (k2); the many person by
the own-form-un-cognition (k3); the Lord's knowledge-action as the animal's guṇas (k4); the power-ness
not from distinction (k5); the being-bliss-action of the Lord and its absence in the animal (k6); the
non-conventional this-ness of the Lord (k7); and the distinct-manifestation-meanings constructed of
the inner-self (k8). The foundation of the collection: all the categories and all the knowers rest in
the one free Lord.
uncertainties: The exact "puruṣa evedaṃ sarvam" and "sarvabhāvāḥ śivaḥ" citations — the Śivadṛṣṭi and the
The sattva/rajas/tamas mapping onto the Lord's powers (k4–6) — the correspondence is Abhinava's;

speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator voice)
question:
The tattvasaṅgraha's middle section (kārikās 9–15) expounds the bond (bandha) and
its relation to the knower and the known. The central problem: the bound knower (paśu) creates his own
world — but how is this creation related to the Lord's creation? And what is the difference between the
bound and the liberated? Kārikās 9–15 answer: the paśu's creation is *asādhāraṇī* (un-common, private),
sustained by the Lord's creation (k9–10); the Lord's own creation is *sādhāraṇā* (common), and through
the abandonment of construction (vikalpahāna) one attains the Lord-ness (k11–12); the known is common,
but the liberated knows it with the own-self-non-difference (k13); in the supreme Śiva there is no
separate known at all (k14); and the fruit is the samyag jñāna-kriyā, the while-living-liberated (k15).
premises:
> "This," indeed, of that, the un-common creation, the Lord-creation-dependent; she-even, with the
> un-knowing-ness, in-the-existing-alone, with the Lord-power, with the that-self —

The paśu's un-common (asādhāraṇī) creation is the Lord-creation-dependent (īśasṛṣṭyujīvinī) — it
subsists on the back of the Lord's creation. It is per-knower, per-time, devoid of other-knower-state-
following. The objection: "if the paśu creates, is it not common like the Lord's?" — No: the paśu's
own power is un-known to him (being other-dependent), and only the Lord-ness awakens it. From the
un-cognition alone comes the bound/liberated-ness. The māyā-power of the Lord — the word-mass body, the
world-re-recollection-form — is the varṇadevatā-wheel, the eight-fold class (vargāṣṭaka), the
ka-and-the-rest syllables; its movement (prāṇāpāna-swing) forbids firmness, and makes the "friend-this,
enemy-this" constructions. The paśu's asādhāraṇī sṛṣṭi depends on the īśvara-created appearances (e.g.
the "ten-tusked elephant"). The sūtra-meaning.

> With the own-rest-obstruction, with the moving, with the breath-form; with the construction-action,
> the that-that-syllable-variety-form —

The construction-action (vikalpakriyā), of the breath-form, is for the obstruction of the own rest. The
māyāśakti (in the māyā-word, the kriyātmikā) binds the paśu (the Spa. 3.16). The kṣetrajña's creations
are sabhittika (based, on the Lord's), not nirbhittika. The varṇadevatās (the ka-and-the-rest) are
the infinite syllable-forms. Even the free constructions (the "king-I-stand") are, on inspection,
parādhīnā (other-dependent). The māyā's three parts (tucchatābhāsa, vaiparītyābhāsa, nañartha) spread
with the three stains.

> The common-alone, the-other, and-the-Lord's-creation, from-the-clear-manifestation; from-the-
> construction-removal, from-the-one-pointedness, by-order, the-Lord-ness-word —

The Lord's creation is clear-manifestation (spaṣṭāvabhāsana), hence un-constructed; it is sādhāraṇa or
asādhāraṇa (the double-moon), both other-than the paśu's creation. When, by the abandonment of
construction and the one-pointedness, the paśu attains the "I-this" Lord-ship-re-recollection, he
destroys his animal-ness and shows the Lord-ness (the Vīrāvalī-Bhairava 113). Even the paśu's creation,
if known with the Lord's power, becomes sādhāraṇa. In the dream, the constructions are clear or
un-clear; the all-known-common-ness. The pratyayasṛṣṭi (the cognition-creation) is the
kārmamalāpyāyikā; the kṣetrajñā's un-freedom (Spa. 3.14). The vikalpanirhrāsa (the thinning of
construction) through the ekāgratā-practice leads to the param-Lord-word; the tattvārthasaṅgraha's
non-repetition; the Vidyā-kalāśaktis; the svabhāvahetu and the pratyakṣa (the agnīndhana example).

> All-mine-this-splendor, thus-of-the-knowing — of-the-world-self, of-the-constructions, in-the-
> spread-even, the-mahā-Lord-ness —

With the thinning of construction and the non-construction-assimilation, the own-cognition is the
liberation (self-manifest). The "not another I" — the grāhyagrāhakaprakāśaghana param-eśvara is the
"aham"; the constructions, fallen into the great re-recollection, become non-construction. The
Pāradarśana ("even doubt is not doubted"); the Śivadṛṣṭi 1.38 (the sārvabhauma king playing the
soldier); the prakṛtitvam-prāptān vikārān ākaroti; the ṛtudhāmā Āditya. The maheśvarataiva (the vṛtti,
the pratyabhijñā).

The mukta, from the Sādākhya-word down to the embryo, knows the mātṛvarga as the "I-this," with the
self-non-difference; the meya is common (mutually and from the knower-group un-distinguished), the
ekarasābhedaviśrānti (the Śivadṛṣṭi 5.106, 7.91, 7.93). The baddha, in the reversal, is the
ekaghanabhedaviśrānta. The tulyam (equal) is the kriyāviśeṣaṇa.

> In-every-way-though-the-inner-dissolved-infinite-category-flood-filled; the-Śiva, the-consciousness-
> bliss-mass, the-param-syllable-form —

In the Sadāśiva-Īśa ground and the jīvanmukti, the known-order was examined; but in the parama-Śiva
there is no known at all. The "sarvathā" (in every way) excludes; the "filled" (nirbhara) is the
param-ness — the "I"-experience alone is filled; the ahaṃpratītir eva pūryate. The cidānandaghana is
the filled "I"-experience; the paramākṣara is explained likewise.

> Thus-the-own-self-of-this, well-the-knowledge-action-two-thus; knowing-the-as-desired-beings,
> seeing, he-knows-and-he-does-and —

The fruit of the four-section teaching: knowing the own-self as the Lord-form, seeing the
knowledge-action powers (not by the Kāpila/Kāṇāda views), one knows and does whatever one wishes — the
jīvanmukta, who at the fall of the body is the param-eśvara. The māyā-word too is the citprakāśa
(deśakālāspṛṣṭa); the sadāśiveśa-form; the Buddhists (the kṣaṇika, the virodhacintā, the
paramāṇusaṅkoca) refuted; the niravabhāsā saṃvid; the ābhāsa-vimarśa stability (the śukti-rajata); the
ekānekarūpatā; the idantāparāmarśa; the aikādhikaraṇya īśvaratā/śivatā; the
paramaśivarūpāntarlīna īśvaratā (Spa. 1.2). The ||3|| colophon.
inference:
Decision for L2
Proceed. The argument is understood: the paśu's creation is private, sustained by the Lord's (k9); the
construction-action, breath-form, is the binding (k10); the Lord's creation is common, and the
abandonment of construction leads to the Lord-ness (k11); the world-self's mahā-Lord-ness (k12); the
known is common, known by the liberated with the own-self-non-difference (k13); in the supreme Śiva
there is no separate known (k14); and the fruit is the samyag jñāna-kriyā and the jīvanmukta (k15).
The bond is the forgetting; the liberation is the recognition.
uncertainties: The "daśaradana" (ten-tusked vs. ten-faced) elephant (k10) — the correct reading is ten-tusked
The exact "sabhittika/nirbhittika" (based/un-based) creations of the kṣetrajña (k10).

speaker: Abhinavagupta closing the IPVV (siddhānta voice, with pūrvapakṣa objections and the vivṛtikāra's lineage-praise)
question: How does the whole teaching close — what is the single recognition-path, and by what transmission does it stand?
premises: The maṅgala opens the close: the unsurpassed form spreading as bliss-sequence, the world held, all nectar borne within and without — the work bows before summing itself.

The triple source is fixed: part from the self, part from the śāstra, part must come from the guru — book-learning without the guru-order is mocked (the śāstra-sight needs the lineage to reach its proper power).

Kārikā 1 announces the path: well-fitted, new, shown for effortless attainment; kārikā 2 gives the lover-analogy (the unrecognized beloved near at hand); kārikā 3 names the author and the purpose (Utpala establishes it for the effortless attainment of people).
Objections are met on the way: the Sāṃkhya/Buddhist/Vaiśeṣika positions, the smoke-fire rule and the wall-like restatement, the threefold ahaṃ-vimarśa gathering pure, mixed and impure states.

The vivṛtikāra praises the lineage in seventeen verses — Varāhagupta, Cukhulaka, Bhūtirāja, Lakṣmaṇagupta, Tryambaka — and hands the work to the Lord with the two colophons (samastanigamana, samāptā).
inference: The closing sum gathers the whole teaching into one transmission — guru, śāstra, self — and one path: recognition itself, effortless, complete, handed on.
uncertainties: Lineage hagiographic details (Śrīkaṇṭhanātha → Durvāsa → Tryambakāditya) — preserved as given, not re-derived.
Print lacunae and wrap-splits (10 AMBIGUOUS L0 rows) — extent unknown, never smoothed.

speaker: Utpaladeva (maṅgala, praise voice)
question: Under what auspice does the Lord's proof open?
premises: He who makes (karoti) — him (tam), I (aham) praise (naumi): the one (ekam) God (devam), Maheśvara the Lord.
The auspice names the conclusion in advance: maker, one, Lord.
inference: Auspice: praise of the one maker-Lord whose proof follows.
uncertainties: Opening pādas lost to print lacuna; the surviving half-verse is complete as praise.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is the inference to be proved?
premises: Bodies and the rest (tanvādi) have conscious cause (buddhimaddhetu), having distinct arrangement (saṃniveśaviśeṣavat).
Like pots (ghaṭa ... like atoms, paramāṇuvat — mid-verse lacuna).
The Nyāya shape is unmistakable: pakṣa (bodies), hetu (arrangement), dṛṣṭānta (pot).
inference: Thesis stated in Nyāya dress: arranged bodies bespeak a conscious maker, like pots.
uncertainties: Mid-verse gap (dots) eats the example's middle; atoms-vs-pot pairing partly lost — read with prose.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What survives of the example's turn?
premises: Urged by the conscious (buddhimat-prorito) — or (vā) ... [lacuna].
Remnant ṭato ([ta]ṭo? — thence?) — pot (ghaṭaḥ), as (yathā).
The yathā-form survives: 'as pot from [tha]t' — example-phrase intact.
inference: Fragment: the example-form (as pot...) survives its verse.
uncertainties: Major lacuna; prorito unattested (pra+√īr?); ṭato unresolved. No doctrine built on remnants.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What survives of the fixed-meaning turn?
premises: ... without arrangement ([saṃ]skāra-saṃsthāna-varjitaḥ?).
Fixed (niścitaḥ) is its meaning (arthaḥ) in locus (saṃsthāne) — in that (tasmin), action-heaped (arthakriyā) ... (cite remnant).
inference: Fragment: fixed meaning in its locus, amid action-heaping.
uncertainties: Leading lacuna; cite isolated (vocative of cita? severed compound?). Held open.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How is the maker marked?
premises: In the varied (vicitre), the conscious alone (buddhimān eva) is marked (lakṣyate) — as among pots (ghaṭādiṣv iva).
The maker (kartā), wise (vijñaḥ), having resolve for varied-this-use (vicitraitadupayogābhisaṃdhimān).
Prose: variety (vaicitrya) is the mark editors of Nyāya-examples read for intelligence.
inference: Variety marks the wise maker: resolved on varied use, visible among pots.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can matter arrange?
premises: There is (asti), in function-yoking (arthakriyāyoge), among bodies and worlds (śarīrabhuvanādiṣu).
This distinct arrangement (ayam saṃniveśaviśeṣaḥ) — not possibly from material (anupādānasaṃbhavī).
inference: Arrangement in function-fit things cannot come from matter alone.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What follows from proved makers?
premises: Then here (tat atra), by proving conscious makers (buddhimatkartṛsiddhyā), Lord-action is proved (siddheśvarakriyā).
For knowers of such variety (tādṛśavaicitryaviduṣaḥ), non-lordliness (anīśitā) is impossible (syāt = would be — denied).
inference: Makers proved prove the Lord's act: variety-knowers cannot be lordless.

speaker: Objector (Nyāya-Buddhist voice; cf. anvaya debates)
question: Does concomitance hold for potter or Lord?
premises: Neither by potter (kulālena) nor by Lord (īśena) is agreement (anvayaḥ) shown here (atra).
Since (yatas) for him there would be either opposition (viruddhatā) or unproved agreement (asiddhānvayatā).
Prose: the stock Nyāya worry — anvaya with an unseen maker is unproved; with a seen one, off-point.
inference: Objection stated: the concomitance fails on both horns — opposition or unprovedness.
uncertainties: Voice attribution (objection vs concession) from prose context; the reply (v09) confirms objector.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What answers the anvaya dilemma?
premises: Merely (kevalam) even from showing (saṃdarśanāt) pervasion (vyāpti) with the conscious alone (buddhimanmātra).
By thesis-property force (pakṣadharmabalāt), somewhere (kvacit), someone (kaścit) wise (dhīmān) is understood (pratīyate).
inference: Reply: bare showing of conscious-only pervasion suffices — by pakṣadharma-force alone, some wise one is grasped. Minimalism against the dilemma.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How is the higher self shown in eye etc.?
premises: As (yathā) combination-ness (saṃghātatva) is seen (anvitekṣite) merely for another's sake (pārārthyamātreṇa).
In eye etc. (cakṣurādau), by that fitness (tadaucityāt): the self-dear (ātmeṣṭaḥ), uncompounded (asaṃhataḥ), higher (paraḥ).
Prose: Sāṅkhya's own eye-example turned — fitness, not assemblage, shows the self-cherished uncompounded.
inference: The higher self shows in eye etc. by fitness, as combination seen for another's sake.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How is fire proved as khadira-wood?
premises: As (yathā) from afar (dūrataḥ), from smoke (dhūmāt), proving (siddhiḥ) in a khadira-grove (khadirakānane).
Fire (vahniḥ) is proved (siddhyati) just by knowing it (tatpratipattyā), as khadira-wood (khādiratvena).
Stock smoke-fire example redeployed: mere knowing-it suffices for wood-kind — no need to see the logs.
inference: Fire is proved as khadira-wood by mere knowing: the stock example turned for fitness.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is the hetu, and what is excluded?
premises: Thus (evam) the cause (hetuḥ): locus-form alone (saṃsthānamātram), here (atra) distinguished (viśeṣitam).
Not (na) by variety merely (vaicitryamātreṇa) as svalakṣaṇa-mark (svalakṣaṇalakṣmaṇā).
Prose: against the Buddhist svalakṣaṇa-only mark — bare variety doesn't mark; the hetu is fenced.
inference: The hetu stated (locus-form alone) and fenced: not bare variety as particular-mark.
uncertainties: svalakṣaṇalakṣmaṇā scope (whose mark?) from prose — read as the Buddhist's mark, refused.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What do others sift?
premises: By others too (paraiḥ taiḥ api), of reasons (hetūnāṃ), in pot-self-sifting (ghaṭātmapravivecane).
Locus-form alone (saṃsthānamātram) ... even (eva) ... [gap] ... causehood (hetutvam) of the conscious-possessor (buddhiśālinaḥ).
inference: Others too sift reasons in pot-self-analysis: bare locus-form [carries] the conscious one's causehood.
uncertainties: Mid-verse gap (eva…); the carried predicate partly lost — read with prose, nothing restored.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What whole is rightly Lord-made?
premises: Mutual-function-fit-locus-formed (anyonyārthakriyāyogyasaṃniveśaviśeṣitam) — that (tat), this (idam) whole (sakalam) world (viśvam).
Rightly (yuktam) Lord-made (īśvaranirmitam).
inference: The mutual-fit world-whole is rightly Lord-made.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What strange way of helpers?
premises: Here it is replied (atrocyate): a strange way (gatiścitrā) of helpers (sahakāriṇām) is seen (dṛśyate).
Some (kecit) somehow (kathaṃcid) would join (eveyuḥ) with materials (upādānaiḥ) — a joining (samāgamam).
Metrically confirmed v15ab (8+8); atrocyate kept as verse-opening reply-formula.
inference: Reply-frame opened: helpers show a strange way — some joining with materials somehow.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How do helpers picture effects?
premises: Helpers (hetumantaḥ), entering (praviśya) as others (anye), reaching (prāpya) material-form (upādānarūpatām).
They picture (citrayanti) effects (kāryāṇi) — like earth-water-juices (bhaumodakarasā iva).
inference: Helpers picture effects by entering-as-other and reaching material-form — like earth-juices.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Are outward-changers capable?
premises: Others (anye), again (punar), in material (upādāne), outward-changing (bahirviparivartinaḥ).
For form-variety-yoking (rūpavaicitryayogāya) in effects (kāryeṣu) — not so (na tathā) capable (kṣamāḥ).
inference: Outward-changers in matter can't yoke form-variety in effects.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Does imagined spread order all?
premises: There (tatra), if (yadi) the conscious one's spread (prasaraḥ) by name (nāma) be imagined (kalpyate).
Not (na) by that much alone (tāvataiva) does order (vyavasthā) hold everywhere (sarvatra) — thus (tathā ghaṭate).
inference: Imagined spread of the conscious doesn't alone order everywhere.

speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
question: How is pradhāna proved?
premises: There is (asti), of this proved (prasiddhasya) pradhāna (pradhānasya), by anvaya and the rest (anvayādinā).
By denial (niṣedhena) of self-aims and the like (svārthatādi), person-aim-ness (puruṣārthatā) is proved (sādhitā).
Prose: Sāṅkhya's satkārya/anvaya apparatus — pradhāna established through concomitance, purposed to spirit.
inference: Sāṅkhya stated: pradhāna proved by anvaya; purposed to spirit by denying self-aims.

speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
question: How easy is change?
premises: Through that (tena), person's (puruṣasya) enjoyment-proving (bhogasaṃsiddhiḥ) — again and again (yathā yathā).
So (tathā tathā), change (pariṇatiḥ) would be (syāt) nothing (na kiṃcana) hard (durghaṭam).
inference: Change comes easy, again and again, for spirit's enjoyment.

speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
question: What moves pradhāna?
premises: Hence indeed (ata eva), for ever-becoming (mahattvapariṇāminaḥ) pradhāna (pradhānasya).
No (na) nimitta-cause (nimittakāraṇaṃ) other (anyat) but (ṛte) person-aim-striving (puruṣārthodyamāt).
inference: Only person-aim-striving moves ever-becoming pradhāna.

speaker: Sāṅkhya (pūrvapakṣin)
question: What is own-nature for?
premises: Own-nature (svabhāvaḥ) indeed (eva) — and (ca) this (eṣaḥ) of this (asya).
From seeing the root-cause then (mūlahetoḥ tatekṣaṇāt); below mind-ground (cittabhūmer adharataḥ), toward body-ordaining (śarīrādi vidhim).
inference: Own-nature faces downward: from root-cause-seeing toward body's ordaining.
uncertainties: tatekṣaṇāt parsed then-seeing (tat+ekṣaṇāt); at-the-moment (tate+kṣaṇāt) equivalent in force — settled.

speaker: Sāṅkhya closing / siddhāntin opening (pivot)
question: As efficient cause (nimittakāraṇaṃ), karma (karma) could be (syāt) even (api) original-natured (ādya-svabhāvataḥ).
Then (tatas) here (atra) — where (kutra) is Īśvara's business (vyāpāraḥ) to be conceived (upakalpyatām)?
Prose: karma-as-nimitta considered and bounded; the question turns the page.
premises: As efficient cause (nimittakāraṇaṃ), karma (karma) could be (syāt) even (api) original-natured (ādya-svabhāvataḥ).
Then (tatas) here (atra) — where (kutra) is Īśvara's business (vyāpāraḥ) to be conceived (upakalpyatām)?
Prose: karma-as-nimitta considered and bounded; the question turns the page.
inference: Pivot: karma admitted as possible nimitta — then where is Īśvara's business?
uncertainties: v23cd read as siddhāntin's programmatic question (answered v24); Sāṅkhya-dismissal reading recorded but set aside — see NOTE.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is to be conceived?
premises: Of secret nature (rahanatvasya — print's (natva) kept), in root-nature (mūlaprakṛtau), protecting (avantaḥ) inner-organ-rangers (karaṇacāriṇaḥ).
Let Īśvara's (īśvarasya) change-causality (pariṇāmanimittatā) be conceived (upakalpyeta).
inference: Proposal: let Īśvara's change-causality be conceived for root-nature's rangers.
uncertainties: rahanatvasya unresolved (rahaḥ? rahana? + natva?) — kept as printed with insertion; sense from prose. Held open.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What example?
premises: If (yadi) of uniform-change-nature (pariṇāmaikasvabhāvaṃ) — then (atha) thence (tataḥ).
Independent (ananyāpekṣi) seed-kitchen (bījādisāmagrī), as (yadvat) in sprout (aṅkure).
inference: Seed-kitchen example: independent, as in sprouts.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What of Sāṅkhya?
premises: The mahad-first-change-torrent-natured (mahadādivikāraughapariṇāmasvabhāvakam), three-natured (triguṇātma) pradhāna-self (pradhānaṃ).
And (ca) thereby (tena): godless (anīśvaram) Sāṅkhya (sāṃkhyam).
inference: Verdict on Sāṅkhya: three-natured pradhāna — thereby godless.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is conceived?
premises: If (cet) puruṣārtha-natured (puruṣārthasvabhāvatvaṃ) in all function-acts (samastārthakriyāsu).
By pradhāna (pradhānasya) it is conceived (upakalpyate) as efficient (nimittakāraṇatvena).
inference: Conditional close: puruṣārtha-natured acts conceived efficient by pradhāna.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Without what no pot?
premises: Without that (tat vinā) — without potter (kumbhakāreṇa) — even a pot (ghaṭo'pi).
How (katham) could it be (bhavet)?
inference: No pot without potter: how else could it be?

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What of clay-lump nature?
premises: From the pradhāna-made clay-lump (pradhānamayamṛtpiṇḍāt) indeed (eva) — of such nature (tādṛksvabhāvataḥ).
Now (atha): own-nature (svabhāvaḥ) — this (eṣaḥ) of this (asya) — which (yat) looks to potter and the rest (kulālādi apekṣaṇam).
inference: Own-nature looks to potter etc.: clay-lump nature potter-watching.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can helpers entering matter arrange?
premises: Not (na) indeed (eva): by entering (praveśāt) inside the material cause (upādānahetvantaḥ), with helpers (sahakāribhiḥ).
Arrangement (saṃniveśaḥ) could (śakyaḥ) be made (kartum), they say (iti) — though able (kṣamam).
Prose: entering doesn't transfer arrangement-making; helpers stay helpers.
inference: Entering matter with helpers can't make arrangement — ability aside.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Without what wisdom?
premises: World-traffic-linking-having (lokayātrānusaṃdhānavatīṃ) wisdom (prajñāṃ) — without (vinā) — not indeed (nahi).
inference: Hemistich as printed: without world-linked wisdom — never.
uncertainties: Hemistich (cd lost in print); nothing restored.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Without desiring?
premises: So (tathā), without (vinā) desiring-to-make (cikīrṣāṃ), no wondrous-making arising (vicitraracanodbhavaḥ).
There'd be mere grossness (sthūlatāmātram), not (na) world-useful (lokopayoginī) — but (tu).
inference: No will, no wonders: mere grossness, never world-good.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: If from potter-helping?
premises: Making (racanā) by rule (niyamena) would be (syāt) wondrous (vicitrā), kind-formed (jātirūpiṇī).
If (cet) from potter-helping-mereness (kulālasahakāritvamātrāt) a pot is born (jāyate ghaṭaḥ).
inference: Conditional: rule-wondrous making — if mere potter-help bore pots.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What of bodies and arrangement?
premises: Never (na) would there be (syāt) body etc. (śarīrādi) — long clay-lump (dīrghamṛtpiṇḍa) or (vā).
Hence (atas) indeed (eva): by being-led-to-the-end (arthanīyatvāt), arrangement (saṃniveśaḥ) excels (viśiṣyate).
inference: No bodies otherwise; end-led arrangement excels.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Lord or non-Lord?
premises: Not (na) by pot-etc.-ness (ghaṭāditayā) proved (siddhaḥ) — the need-fulfiller (arthitāparipūrakaḥ).
Neither Lord (īśvaraḥ) nor non-Lord (anīśvaraḥ) is taken (prakṛtaḥ) here (atra) as atomic-marked (aṇulakṣaṇaḥ).
inference: Both extremes fenced: neither Lord nor un-Lord atomically taken.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Does pradhāna will?
premises: Nor (na) of pradhāna (pradhānasya) desire-etc.-arising (icchādi saṃbhavaḥ)...
person-aim-ness (puruṣārthatā).
inference: Pradhāna will-less — yet person-aim-ness stands.
uncertainties: na-scope ambiguous (denies arising? or denies puruṣārthatā?); read as fencing will off pradhāna, keeping puruṣārthatā — held open.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Unperceived arising — whose purpose?
premises: Buddhi's arising-or-not (saṃbhavan apy asaṃbhavī).
Without spirit-perceptibility (vinā saṃvedyatāṃ puṃsaḥ).
In such a state (tathātve).
inference: No puruṣārthatā where no spirit perceives (sentence completes in v38).
uncertainties: Cross-verse sentence: bare puruṣārthatā completes in v38's avācyā — read together.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Unspeakable — of whom?
premises: Even of spirit, even of pradhāna — unspeakable (puṃso'pi syāt pradhānasyāvācyā).
Of the mere (kevalasya tu).
Yet mind's/buddhi's function is individually conditioned (athāpi manaso vṛttir buddher vā ekaikasaṃskṛtā).
inference: Denial stands; the concession is the objector's best case, pressed in v39.
uncertainties: cd concedes the objector's best case (individual conditioning) to press it in v39.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How could will serve all?
premises: Will, indeed — how serve all spirits' purposes (icchā nāma kathaṃ sarvapuruṣārthopayoginī syāt)?
The escape: it belongs to generic pradhāna, for all (kiṃ tu sā pradhānasya sāmānyasya akhilān prati).
inference: The how-question marks the generic-will escape, demolished in v40.
uncertainties: kiṃ-tu pivots to the generic-pradhāna escape, demolished in v40.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Perceived — by whom?
premises: Even unperceived by spirit, could it be? Not will (puṃso'pi syāt…asaṃvedyā na…icchā).
Perceived — by whom would it be (vedyā ca kasya sā)?
If by all: omniscience of each follows (yadi sarveṣāṃ sārvajñyam ekaikasya prasajyate).
inference: Generic will forces omniscience on each — reductio.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin, voicing the escape)
question: One light — whose divisions?
premises: Through light-unity the distinct appearances would mix (saṃkīryeran prakāśaikyāt bhinnāś cābhāsamānatāḥ).
The escape: by some One undivided from all spirits (athāpi sarvapuruṣābhinnena ekena kenacit).
inference: The escape becomes the Īśvara-turn (prose: tatsa eveśvaro'stu).
uncertainties: cd — the objector's escape that becomes the Īśvara-turn; voice held as siddhāntin-voiced.

speaker: Pūrvapakṣin (svabhāva-vādin)
question: Seed to sprout — by what purpose?
premises: Not from world-sustenance-purpose would it produce seed into sprout (na lokayātrābhiprāyāt janayed bījam aṅkuram).
But by nature — such a kit is its cause, of such a kind (kiṃ tu svabhāvāt sā tasya sāmagrī hetur īdṛśaḥ).
inference: Nature's kit suffices — the svabhāva position stated.

speaker: Pūrvapakṣin (svabhāva-vādin)
question: Purpose-speech — by what right?
premises: What is born, fit — the wise man joins to one another (yaj jātaṃ yogyam anyonyaṃ yojayed buddhimāñ janaḥ).
By this courtesy, puruṣārthatva is said of it (asya tena upacāreṇa puruṣārthatvam ucyate).
inference: Purpose is courtesy-speech — the thread v44 pulls.
uncertainties: upacāra-concession: puruṣārthatva merely metaphorical — the thread pulled in v44.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Granted — then what, for the freed?
premises: If thus (iti cet).
Even on completion, even in purpose (tat samāptau api puruṣārthe api).
Toward him — the freed spirit (taṃ prati).
inference: The grant suspends; the blow lands in v45.
uncertainties: Protasis suspends; apodosis lands in v45.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Ceaseless churning — whose liberation?
premises: From own-effect-change the root-cause would not cease (svakāryapariṇāmāt na viramen mūlakāraṇam).
Oh — it does not cease (āho na viramati).
This beyond, in nature's seven (etat paraṃ prakṛtisaptake).
inference: Nature-alone never releases — hence a perceiving maker (v52).
uncertainties: āho ironic — the objector's triumph voiced to collapse it; drives to v52's buddhimatkartṛ.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Desired by all — yet whose change?
premises: From change, that One is desired for all spirits (pariṇāmāt tad ekaṃ hi sarvān puṃsaḥ pratīṣyate).
Yet body-earth-and-rest's change is by nature (tathāpi dehabhūtādeḥ pariṇāmaḥ svabhāvataḥ).
inference: The grant (all desire the One) pressed by the body-case.
uncertainties: taye pāṭhāntara for tathāpi in apparatus — sense stable under either; print reading kept.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Why not for the deemed-freed?
premises: As before — why would it not be, toward the deemed-freed (pūrvavan na bhavet kasmāt taṃ muktābhimataṃ prati)?
Yet it does occur — but is not joined by him (athāpi sa bhavaty eva kiṃ tu tena na yujyate).
inference: Occurrence without union — the freed-spirit test.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Needlessness — whose?
premises: By the freed spirit — done with tasks, need-free — he stands alone (mukta-puṃsā kṛtārthatvād anarthitvāt sa kevalaḥ).
Not so: needlessness belongs to no spirit ever, nor to mind (naitan nārthitvam asyāsti jātu puṃso'tha cetasaḥ).
inference: The objector's need-free spirit denied on both sides.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: No reunion — and yet born?
premises: With need gone, no meeting with spirit again would be (arthitvavigamān na syād bhūyaḥ puṃsā samāgamaḥ).
This too is unjust, once body-dwelling mind is born (tad etad api na nyāyyaṃ jāte dehasthacetasi).
inference: Liberation-by-needlessness contradicts rebirth.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Mokṣa — nature or karma's end?
premises: If from perceptible-only-nature of that, not from karma's waning (saṃvedyaikasvabhāvatvāt tasya karmakṣayān na cet).
Mokṣa would be mere nature, resting on karma's waning (tat svabhāvatvam eva syān mokṣaḥ karmakṣayāśrayaḥ).
inference: The view collapses mokṣa into nature.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Mercy-acts — passionless?
premises: There'd be acts even of spirit-distinction-knowers, from compassion (syur jñātapuṃvivekānāṃ karmāṇy api kṛpāditaḥ).
If not from passion — thus mokṣa from passion's exhaustion (na rāgāt tāni ced evaṃ mokṣo rāgakṣayād bhavet).
inference: Compassion smuggles passion back; the view becomes passion-exhaustion doctrine.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Abandoned — what stands?
premises: Thus view-abandoned — that nature-view is unjust (tathā ca darśanatyāgas tan na yuktā svabhāvadṛk).
Hence body-and-rest, famously, have sentient-maker as prior (tasmāt prasiddhaṃ tanvādi buddhimatkartṛpūrvakam).
inference: The siddhānta: bodies bespeak a knowing maker.
uncertainties: svabhāvadṛk agrees with yuktā (the abandoning is nature-viewed).

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Proved — by what?
premises: From setup-difference (saṃsthānabhedāt).
This flawless proof (ity etan niravadyaṃ prasādhanam).
inference: Arrangement-difference seals the design inference.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Aimed at whom — shaken by what?
premises: This reason, aimed at the Supreme Lord by the self-entrusted self (sa eṣa hetuḥ parameśvaraṃ prati prayujyamānaḥ svaniveśitātmanā).
Not overpowered by reason-faults in the least (na hetudoṣaiḥ paribhūyate manāk).
Nor the rival's either — only this is said (paro'pi vā kevalam etad ucyate).
inference: The hetu stands aimed at the Lord; rivals answered, disputation closed.
uncertainties: kevalam-etad-ucyate scope: 'only this is said' closes the disputation.

speaker: Utpaladeva (closing)
question: Proved — yet for whom in vain?
premises: Though proved by a thousand blazing reasons (samujjvalan nyāyasahasrasādhito'py upaiti).
It succeeds not for the deluded-minded (siddhiṃ na vimūḍhacetasām).
Maheśvara, placed on the palm, yet flees the fate-struck — the true jewel (maheśvaraḥ pāṇitalasthito'pi san palāyate daivahatasya sanmaṇiḥ).
inference: Proof needs fitness; the jewel flees the fated.

speaker: Utpaladeva (signature)
question: Who shines within — and who signs?
premises: One's own self indeed — this — flashes forth: Īśvara within all breathers (svātmaivāyaṃ sphurati sakalaprāṇinām īśvaro'ntaḥ).
Maker and knower too (kartā jñātāpi ca).
Yet recognition of the beyond is to be effected (yadi paraṃ pratyabhijñāsya sādhyā).
And the joining is made by us elsewhere (sā cāsmābhir vihitaghaṭanānyatra).
But Īśvara-proved stands even in duality (kiṃ tv īśasiddhir dvaite'py asti).
Fitting, and more: fire shines at midnight (ity ucitam adhikaṃ bhāti vahnir niśīthe).
inference: Self is Īśvara within all; the proof stands even dualist; signature and forward glance.
uncertainties: pratyabhijñā-program link: recognition to be effected — the work's forward glance to the Īśvarapratyabhijñā; joining 'made by us elsewhere' points outside this treatise.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What rite ends sorrow?
premises: Completion-rite amid sorrow's host, in spreading bliss-taste, on a foul day.
By mutual doing, in the weighty Lord's hymn (uneven-flame scorcher), mind ever mirrors back.
Seal: fear gone.
inference: The hymn mirrors back the fearful mind into fearlessness.
uncertainties: Long-compound syntax held as printed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: How is hymning effortless?
premises: Examined self examines again the hymned conduct; worshipper presents in hymn amid difference-taken-as-one.
Examined self at every object-knowing moment: 'thus in Your hymn I stand here always, effortless.'
inference: Self-examination redoubled makes hymning effortless.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What if the self goes unscrutinized?
premises: Unscrutinized self never shares thing-knowing; unscrutinized, without grasping-course, it is not.
But Śiva — that self shining, one sap of all things — hence I, heart-devoted, ever blissful in Your hymn.
inference: Unscrutinized, no knowing; scrutinized, Śiva shining one-sapped — bliss.
uncertainties: 'marśanavidhi elision kept; asau demonstrative force.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice, addressing heart)
question: O heart, what now?
premises: By varied birth-wandering gears, omniscience gained — O heart — effortlessly by You.
That within, in teaching-spread-course-become light: clearly in speech obtained — show the Lord's hymn now.
inference: Omniscience gained effortlessly; heart bidden to show the hymn in speech.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice, intoxicated)
question: What does the shaken-off sing?
premises: Shaking off bond-conceit-path-standing, relishing this, difference burnt in endless praise-fire.
From varied self-swelling glory's rushing start, drinking things — O giver — mad-drunk am I, blissful.
inference: Bond burnt, glory rushed, things drunk: madness-bliss sings.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice, questioning)
question: If the heart holds His conduct, how hymn — and by what means?
premises: Be the heart holds the Lord's varied conduct — if so, how would hymning be done? Yet done it is, by that, suddenly.
On Śiva-oneness gained, Śiva-bowing is the first means.
inference: Held conduct unhymnable yet hymned: sudden Śiva-bowing, first means.
uncertainties: yadi-tataḥ-kathaṃ chain kept as staged perplexity.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What body has fire apart from burning?
premises: Flame-formed, ripening-glorious: burning shown, other of fire shed — what body holds at all?
Answer: I praise knowing-rays; if own-each by that praised, none else is the Lord's power.
inference: Fire apart from burning is nobodies: praise knowing-rays, each-owned.
uncertainties: Rhetorical kim api kept; nijanijān distributive.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What taste has the beginningless?
premises: In varied beginningness, melted rule: what taste from partitionlessness — supreme fullness unequalled?
Answer: self's light-yoking, all-thing-oneness, by unopposed dharma-floods: supreme knowing, priceless-fit-qualified (SD aviruddhair).
inference: Partitionless taste, unopposed floods: supreme knowing priceless.
uncertainties: aviruddhair SD over print viruddhair (sense requires unopposed).

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: How shall heart and speech hymn difference-gone form?
premises: Thus in such forms, giver, varied Your form shines — in own-portion this world, difference gone, of the Lord.
May heart to praise that same, and outer-speech-instrument songs, mine constantly, unabandoned-rush.
inference: Difference-gone form shines; heart-and-speech vowed unabandoned.
uncertainties: evaitatstotuṃ print joint kept (SD splits).

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What rises-sets at once within You alone?
premises: Within You-alone-one, throbbing-glory knowledge-ocean, wave-taste spreading by own taste.
They — creations-keepings-dissolvings-formed, moon-sun-fire clash-gleams at once: rise-set powers (SD tavaikasyāntaḥ variant).
inference: Ocean within; moon-sun-fire rise-set at once.
uncertainties: Print tavaivaikasyāntaḥ followed; SD variant noted.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: Where shall the heart fix?
premises: The Lord's power, enjoying varied-unvaried-course and beyond-difference stations, ever goes, never into division, nohow.
So on this unagitated ground — Your step it is — may my heart-ground grow one-pointed, Bhairava Lord.
inference: Power walks undivided; heart prays one-pointed on still ground.
uncertainties: citrācitra stations unexplained, kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: How does freedom meet difference?
premises: From the complete Whole — oh, joy-taste juice — You lead Your own power into difference, by will's spreading.
Priceless Your freedom — praising Your wonder-become power, fear melted, I am Śiva-made.
inference: Whole leads power into difference; praise melts fear into Śiva-made.
uncertainties: vata exclamation kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: How stand that form?
premises: Thisness-just Your form, Lord, power-juiced; by sequencelessness itself time-reckoning forcibly melted.
By mind-power, speech too, sense-wheels, pots outside — may I stand that form at once, unceasing.
inference: Thisness-form power-juiced; sequencelessness melts time; all instruments at once.
uncertainties: idantāvat force kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: How become triple-formed?
premises: You swell sequence on that ground, mete Your powers' difference — show always in Yourself, O god.
Then named doing-knowing-willing, maintenance-dissolution-great-emission-powered, three-formed — may I become, for overlying, eager-hearted.
inference: He swells and shows; prayer to become triple for overlaying.
uncertainties: samadhiśayitum as overlay kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: Where shall emission sport?
premises: Before, emission dissolved, fire-made — where would it shine, facing beyond-joy? Moon-touch-lovely it goes.
O Bhairava Lord — may this emission-named of Yours sport always in my mind.
inference: Dissolved emission questioned; moon-lovely answer; ever-sport prayed.
uncertainties: parollāsaunmukhyaṃ kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: How red?
premises: In emitted thing-share outside, in extreme taste-bliss, You resort by rush to redness-made.
Then red goddess, Yours in all things — make me, by red-drinking-order-joined conclave, past-loathing.
inference: Rush to redness; past-loathing in red rite prayed.
uncertainties: ghṛṇā double sense (loathing/compassion) held; nanu as prayer-particle.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What shall the goddess grasp?
premises: To quit outer work, dwell in noble knowing-ground; show thing-nondifference, waves gone fickle.
Goddess grasps maintenance's end; may she ever grasp my wandering state's undoing, Lord.
inference: Quit outer, dwell noble, show undivided; grasp ends — maintenance's and mine.
uncertainties: vinaṣṭormicapalaḥ kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: How is world-fear ground?
premises: Wishing calm by world-loosing: rule of doubt-fear, then ban — shown; Yama emitted.
Splitting doubt again — may the great goddess grind my world-fear.
inference: Rule-then-ban shown, Yama made, doubt split: grind world-fear.
uncertainties: vidhi/niṣedha pair kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What survives melting?
premises: Doubt-heap melted, conduct gone, glory gone, rule gone — all melted.
Hunger remains: to gulp the endless feast — strike, dissolution-named, my heart's split part.
inference: All melted but hunger: strike prayed.
uncertainties: laṃpaṭarasā kept raw.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: Who makes death-dissolution?
premises: By goddesses at once, difference-glory split — thought-living one shines, knower-standing. Enough.
Considered in own heart, dissolution-formed, gracious — my death-loosing maker, blessed Lady.
inference: Goddesses split difference; thought shines; considered maker gracious.
uncertainties: mātṛsthiti kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What do the three ordain?
premises: So your three, by own-power-expanse-force obtained, six-wheel-course-made-step powers these.
By order, by unfolding, they ordain varied world-state; by these goddesses, devoted-hearted may I be, fear-gone.
inference: Three obtained ordain by unfolding; devotee prays fear-gone by them.
uncertainties: tisraḥ feminine (powers) kept.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee voice)
question: What ground holds, and what conduct sports?
premises: This ground she holds — world-fear-splitting-dread-making; this wake-one-pointed-melted-taste-formed — ordained too.
So holding, melting, wiping inauspicious stretches, as-pleased conduct resorted — may she sport in my heart.
inference: Ground held dread-making; conduct as-pleased sporting in heart prayed.

question: Can ordinary action-based agency apply to an all-pervading self without vibration?
premises: Ordinary agency is established through connection with action.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How do opponents define agency in the self without invoking vibration?
premises: Opponents propose knowledge, desire to act, and effort as a triad.
This triad is said to belong to the self.
They identify the possession of this triad as agency.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How does the author evaluate the opponent's definition of agency?
premises: The proposed definition is presented as misleading.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why does the triad of knowledge, desire, and effort fail to define agency?
premises: Knowledge by itself is not agency because it is present everywhere.
Desire and effort are also generally present in many cases.
What is widely present without producing action cannot be the defining mark of agency.
inference: Therefore, the mere presence of knowledge, desire, and effort does not constitute agency.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Can knowledge, desire, and effort by themselves produce an action?
premises: A potter may know, desire, and make effort to have a house.
Despite possessing these three, he may still fail to make a house for himself.
Agency requires more than the mere presence of the triad.
inference: Therefore, knowledge, desire, and effort are insufficient to constitute real agency.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Does lack of know-how explain why the potter cannot build the house?
premises: An opponent may claim the potter does not know how to do it.
From that lack of know-how, desire and effort would also be absent.
If the relevant know-how is absent, the action cannot occur.
inference: The objection tries to preserve the triad theory by saying the potter lacks the specific knowledge of doing.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What does the qualifier 'to do' add to knowledge, desire, and effort?
premises: The opponent qualifies knowledge, desire, and effort with the phrase 'to do'.
This qualifier must have a determinate meaning.
One possible meaning is that it implies vibration or dynamic activity.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: If 'to do' means vibration, where is that vibration located in an all-pervading self?
premises: If agency means vibration, the self would know and desire to vibrate.
Any such vibration would have to be located in the self.
An all-pervading self, by its nature, does not admit such produced vibration.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Can knowledge without vibration explain agency even in the highest subject?
premises: Knowledge entirely without vibration is not admissible, even for Śiva.

question: What does the phrase 'of the self, to do' amount to when analyzed?

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Does analyzing 'to do' into separate mental acts yield real agency?
premises: Taken individually, the analysis yields knowing to do and desiring to do.

A verbal analysis of 'to do' does not by itself produce agency.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: If agency is only mental, how can bodily and verbal actions belong to the agent?

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

premises: If proximity to qualities were enough, agency could arise even in liberation.

A theory that yields agency in liberation or by another's qualities is unacceptable.
inference: Therefore, proximity to qualities cannot be the basis of agency.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What further doctrinal faults follow from mislocating agency in selves?
premises: If agency is wrongly assigned among selves, karmic accounting breaks down.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

premises: Ordinary agents like potters contribute only a partial causal factor.

premises: True agency consists only in knowledge, will, and effort.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

premises: The wise know that the Lord's autonomy is agency.

premises: Actions do not arise for bondage by their own nature.
