question: Is the joining only thought's fabrication?
premises: This (etat) is no mere thought (na kalpanāmātram): it cannot be warded off (avāraṇāt).
Like snake-error (sarpabhrānteḥ iva): its remedy fails (nivāraṇam) through clinging to a shining (ābhāsalagnatvāt).
Prose (p.5): even your side admits error clinging to thing-shining, unuprootable by refutation.
inference: Retorsion begins: unwardability proves the joining is no mere fabrication.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What makes error stick?
premises: Clinging-to-shining (ābhāsalagnatvam) is not thing-resembling-shining (ābhāsasadṛśārthatā).
It is following-after-shining (ābhāsānusāritvaṃ): error is just that — an erred shining (bhrānta ābhāsa eva tat).
Prose (p.5): all errors concern resembling — but beyond resembling, errors hold by shining-clinging; else the silver-shell could not guide. Transaction-guiding seeming must follow the shining.
inference: Error sticks by following shining, not resembling things: seeming that guides must trail being.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Can this justification be stated?
premises: Thus (ittham), in this very shining (asmin), such unity-seeing of the many (anekasyaikatādṛśi).
Its statable justification (vācyopapattiḥ) too is told (uktā), clearly (sphuṭam), in recognition's path (pratyabhijñānaye).
inference: Warrant claimed: the many-seen-as-one is statable inside the Pratyabhijñā, plainly.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What of consciousness-bodied beings?
premises: Thus (evam), of beings (vastūnāṃ), of consciousness-bodied (cinmātravapuṣāṃ), of beings (satām).
Of Māyā-made-difference (māyānirmitabhedānām) even (api), unity (ekatvam) is not hard to effect (adurghaṭam).
inference: Even Māyā-differenced beings take unity without strain — for the consciousness-bodied.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: What is reflection's object for the worldly?
premises: Therein too (tatrāpi), what (yaḥ) is reflection's object (parāmarśaviṣayaḥ) for the worldly (laukikasya).
That (saḥ): of the knower (vedituḥ) whose pith (sāra) is difference (bheda) of non-difference-shining form (cidabhedaprathārūpa).
inference: The worldly one's reflection-object is the knower whose pith is difference in non-difference-shining form.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Does blocked activity touch another thought?
premises: Activity (vyāpāraḥ) by this (anena) blocked (ruddhaḥ) — it (asau) should touch (spṛśet) no other thought (vikalpāntaram).
For on touching another thought (vikalpāntarasaṃsparśe) follows knower-difference (mātṛbhedaprasaṅgataḥ).
inference: One reflection's business touches no other thought, or knowers multiply.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How do the many reach unity?
premises: Abiding in that-one-reflection (tadekāmarśavarti), by one-word-superimposition force (ekaśabdādhyāsavaśāt).
The many (anekaḥ) too would go (vrajet) to unity (ekatām) — as pot-cloth (ghaṭapaṭau) means (iti).
Prose: dvandva discussed at length — one reflection makes one word, one word one thing.
inference: Many reach oneness through one-word superimposition — 'pot-cloth'.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Is there another relation?
premises: Thus (iti) there is (asti) also (tāvat?) another (anyaḥ): qualifier-qualified (viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyayoḥ) relation (saṃbandhaḥ).
For helping (upakārārthaḥ); it serves (upayujyate) for knowing (jñātum).
inference: A second relation stands: qualifier-qualified, for helping, serving knowledge.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: Is there twoness in manyness?
premises: Even in manyness (bahutve'pi), twoness (dvitvam) would be (bhavet).
From double-reflection birth (dvivimarśabhuvaḥ) — as the king's horses-chariots-men (rājño'śvarathapattayaḥ).
inference: Manyness still yields twoness, double-reflection-born — like the king's retinue.
uncertainties: dvivimarśabhuvaḥ case read ablative (from); genitive ('of') equivalent in sense — settled.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
question: How do the two reflections divide?
premises: Reflection (vimarśaḥ) 'of king' (rājñaḥ iti) is one (ekaḥ), facing own-generality (svasāmānyonmukhaḥ).
The other (paraḥ) — 'man' (puruṣaḥ iti), this (ayam), with master-generality-relation (svāmisāmānyasaṃbandhasahaḥ).
inference: 'King' faces own-generality; 'man' faces the master's — two reflections, one relation.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

premises: 'The king's man' (rājñaḥ puruṣaḥ iti) — this (eṣaḥ), after (paścāt), in relation's range (saṃbandhagocaraḥ).
Is to be thought (kalpyaḥ) by this (anena); or the former two to be thought (kalpyau) — those three (trayaḥ) in every way (sarvathā).
Prose: whole-thought after relation, or part-thoughts — three thinkings, all told.
inference: Three thinkings: whole after relation, or the former two — all told.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

inference: Genitive-relation settles in the qualifier, reaches oneness, keeps own form.

speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)

uncertainties: ekahānyā obscure (with-one-short? one short of what?) — held open as printed; no smoothing.

inference: Other chiefs, other unities: secondary's relation-called — king's horse, man.

inference: Name-catalogue bowed; mantra-bodied kept indefinite (kasmai cid).

inference: Dread fuel, kind flame: the offering is the burnt world.

question: What marks Him?

To God, to gracious some Śambhu — homage.

inference: Veda-foe and Veda-maker at once; hidden mastery bowed.

To hard-to-win Śiva Thee.

premises: The unsurpassed supreme abode is called Akula.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

What is knowable becomes clear and manifest.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How does the power of will give rise to the state of the letter ya?
premises: The power of will exists in two modes, stirred and unstirred.
It turns toward a portion of a different power.
Through that orientation it becomes the state of ya.

Through that turning it becomes ra and la.

sarvatra bahumānena yāpyutkrāntirvimuktaye — everywhere with honor which even departure — for liberation: is departure honored everywhere as liberation?
inference: Question: is honored departure everywhere liberation?

speaker: Teacher (where would God go?)
question: Where could the all-pervading go?
premises: proktā sā sāraśāstreṣu bhogopāyatayoditā — taught she in the essence-śāstras, as enjoyment-means arisen.
yadi sarvagatā devo vadotkramya kva yāsyati — if all-pervading is God — tell! having departed, where will he go?
inference: If God is everywhere, departure goes nowhere: the utkrānti paradox.

speaker: Teacher (pot-like God?)
question: Is God partial?
premises: athāsarvagatastarhi ghaṭatulyastadā bhavet — but if not all-pervading, then pot-like then he would be.
utkrāntividhiyogo 'yamekadeśena kathyate — the departure-rite-yoga — this partially — is taught: partial teaching for a partial God?
inference: Dilemma: all-pervading (no departure) or pot-like (partial rite).

speaker: Teacher (partless, no departure)
question: How depart from the partless?
premises: niraṃśe śivatattve tu kathamutkrāntisaṃgatiḥ — but in the partless Śiva-principle, how departure-fittingness?
yathā dharādau vāyvante bhṛgvambvagnyupavāsakaiḥ — as from earth-and-the-rest to wind-end, by cliff-water-fire fasts (reading flagged).
inference: No departure fits the partless; cliff-water-fire fasts don't either.
uncertainties: bhṛgvambvagnyupavāsakaiḥ — flagged.

speaker: Teacher (don't eject the soul)
question: Should the soul be ejected?
premises: ātmano yojanaṃ vyomni tadvadutkrāntivartanā — of the self joining in the void, likewise departure-procedure.
tasmānnotkramayejjīvaṃ paratattvasamīhayā — therefore one should not make the soul depart out of longing for the supreme principle.
inference: Don't eject the soul out of longing: prohibition of willed departure.

speaker: Teacher (Pūrvaśāstra's definition)
question: What did the Pūrvaśāstra define?
premises: śrīpūrvaśāstre tūktaṃ yadutkrānterlakṣaṇaṃ na tat — but in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra, whatever of departure the mark was told — not that.
muktyupāyatayā kiṃtu bhogahānyai tathaiṣaṇāt — as a means to liberation; but for loss of enjoyment, from such desiring: departure defined as enjoyment-loss, not liberation.
inference: Pūrvaśāstra: utkrānti defined for enjoyment-loss, not liberation.

speaker: Teacher (detached may leave)
question: Who may leave the body?
premises: japadhyānādisaṃsiddhaḥ svātantryācchaktipātataḥ — perfected by japa-meditation-and-the-rest, through freedom, from śaktipāta.
bhogaṃ prati viraktaśceditthaṃ dehaṃ tyajediti — toward enjoyment detached, if thus: the body should abandon — quoted permission.
inference: The detached perfected one may abandon the body: permission, not prescription.

speaker: Teacher (Bhīṣma precedent)
question: What of Bhīṣma?
premises: svacchandamṛtyorapi yad bhīṣmādeḥ śrūyate kila — even of self-willed death, what from Bhīṣma onward is heard, indeed.
bhogavairasyasaṃprāptau jīvitāntopasarpaṇam — on arrival at enjoyment-distaste: approaching life's end.
inference: Bhīṣma precedent: self-willed death on enjoyment-distaste.

speaker: Teacher (siddhi-body stays)
question: Can the siddhi-body be shed?
premises: yogamantrāmṛtadravyavarādyaiḥ siddhibhāktanuḥ — by yoga-mantra-nectar-substance-boon-and-the-rest, a siddhi-partaking body.
hātuṃ nahyanyathā śakyā vinoktakramayogataḥ — to abandon: for not otherwise is possible without the stated-sequence-practice.
inference: The siddhi-made body can't be shed except by the stated sequence.

speaker: Teacher (deem enjoyment ugly)
question: What does the Mālinītantra add?
premises: uktaṃ ca mālinītantre parameśena tādṛśam — and told in the Mālinītantra by the Supreme Lord likewise.
sarvamapyathavā bhogaṃ manyamāno virūpakam — all even — or else — enjoyment deeming ugly: deem all enjoyment ugly.
inference: Mālinītantra: deem all enjoyment ugly — the same doctrine.

speaker: Teacher (freedom taught in duties)
question: What is the teaching?
premises: ityādi vadatā sarvairalakṣyāntaḥsatattvakam — 'thus and the rest,' by one who says: by all, the inner-reality-unseen reality (provisional).
evaṃ sṛṣṭyādikartavyasvasvātantryopadeśanam — thus: teaching of one's own freedom in creation-and-the-rest duties.
inference: The teaching: one's own freedom in all duties, reality unseen by all.
uncertainties: antaḥsatattvakam split provisional — flagged.

speaker: Teacher (chief dīkṣā)
question: What is the chief initiation?
premises: yatsaiva mukhyadīkṣā syācchiṣyasya śivadāyinī — which very chief initiation should be of the disciple, Śiva-giving.
uktaṃ śrīniśicāre ca bhairavīyeṇa tejasā — told in the venerable Niśicāra, and by Bhairavī energy, radiance.
inference: Chief dīkṣā: the freedom-teaching, Śiva-giving, Bhairavī-radiant.

speaker: Teacher (thought-free beholds)
question: Who beholds the pervaded universe?
premises: vyāptaṃ viśvaṃ prapaśyanti vikalpojjhitacetasaḥ — pervaded, the universe they behold: the thought-abandoned-minded.
vikalpayuktacittastu piṇḍapātācchivaṃ vrajet — but the thought-joined-minded: from body's fall, Śiva reaches.
inference: Thought-free behold now; thought-bound reach Śiva at death.

speaker: Teacher (jīvanmukta now)
question: Who is liberated alive?
premises: bāhyadīkṣādiyogena caryāsamayakalpanaiḥ — by outer-initiation-and-the-rest-practice, through conduct-samaya-constructs.
avikalpastathādyaiva jīvanmukto na saṃśayaḥ — thought-free, just so, now indeed: living-liberated, no doubt.
inference: Thought-free now: living-liberated, no doubt.

speaker: Teacher (fire-mass blazes)
question: What blazes at the end?
premises: saṃsārajīrṇatarumūlakalāpakalpasaṃkalpasāntaratayā — by thought made like the root-mass of the world-worn-out tree, inwardly.

paramārthavahneḥ syurvisphuliṅgakaṇikā api cettadante dedīpyate vimalabodhahutāśarāśiḥ — of the ultimate fire: may there be spark-fragments; even if at its end, blazes intensely the pure-awakening-fire-mass.
inference: Even spark-fragments of the burnt world-tree blaze into the pure-awakening-fire-mass.

speaker: Teacher (approach shown)
question: What closes?
premises: itthaṃ dīkṣopakramo 'yaṃ darśitaḥ śāstrasaṃmataḥ — thus the initiation-approach, this, shown, scripturally approved: colophon.
inference: Colophon: the initiation-approach shown, scriptures concurring.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How does initiation function as the means for both enjoyment and liberation?
premises: A sacrifice is first explained for its practical use.
In that context initiation is presented as the central means.
Initiation serves as the means for both enjoyment and liberation.
inference: Therefore initiation is established as the primary means leading to both worldly enjoyment and liberation.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is a candidate directed toward the enjoyments he desires through initiation?
premises: Initiation works either directly or through consecration.
A candidate may desire specific enjoyments in a particular domain.
The candidate is appointed precisely in that domain.
inference: Therefore initiation directs each candidate to the domain of the enjoyments he seeks.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What determines where a candidate is placed so that he attains success through mantra power?
premises: The revered Svayambhuva scripture states that one becomes a partaker of success through mantra power.
Placement depends on the candidate's fitness.
A candidate is placed where his inclination lies.
inference: Therefore fitness and inclination determine the placement that leads to success through mantra power.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why does the teacher in the Malinimata present initiation as a means beyond mere enjoyment?
premises: A properly appointed candidate does not fall away from his path.
The Malinimata declares initiation to be a means for enjoyment and more.
The teacher does not limit initiation to enjoyment alone.
inference: Therefore initiation is taught as a means that extends beyond enjoyment to higher aims.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Does initiation grant only eligibility for yoga in the Shaiva path?
premises: There is no eligibility for Shaiva yoga without initiation.
Initiation does not produce only eligibility for yoga.
Initiation has broader effects than a single qualification.
inference: Therefore initiation is necessary for Shaiva yoga but its effect is not limited to yoga eligibility alone.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What direct result does Shiva initiation produce according to the Malini statement?
premises: Shiva initiation grants eligibility for mantra.
Shiva initiation grants liberation.
The Malini statement presents initiation as a direct means to liberation.
inference: Therefore Shiva initiation is taught as a direct means to liberation as well as to mantra eligibility.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: In what indirect way can initiation serve as a means to both liberation and enjoyment?
premises: Earlier texts have already spoken about initiation.
Initiation can operate through a transmitted process of consecration.
Through that process it becomes a means to liberation and enjoyment.
inference: Therefore initiation can function indirectly, through consecration in succession, as a means to both liberation and enjoyment.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What provision is made for those who are determined but incapable of the path of knowledge?
premises: Some candidates are determined but lack the capacity for knowledge.
An easier means is available for such candidates.
The teacher has declared a procedure suited to them.
inference: Therefore those incapable of the knowledge path are given an easier procedure by the teacher.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is knowledge described as a direct means to liberation in the Matanga scripture?
premises: The Matanga scripture speaks of the means to liberation.
Knowledge is defined as having the nature of right understanding.
Such knowledge liberates directly.
inference: Therefore knowledge is presented in the Matanga as the direct means to liberation.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Where is the liberating role of knowledge clearly explained in relation to the principles?
premises: The same scripture discusses the principles in terms of cause and effect.
That discussion distinguishes what is to be rejected and accepted.
The knowledge section states this clearly.
inference: Therefore the knowledge section clearly explains how understanding the principles leads to liberation.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What path is prescribed for those incapable of knowledge, and who is considered supreme?
premises: Some candidates are incapable of the direct path of knowledge.
For them initiation, conduct, and absorption are prescribed.
These are properly preceded by knowledge, making the knower supreme.
inference: Therefore even the graded path for the incapable depends on knowledge, and the knower is supreme.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is initiation required before one can receive knowledge from scripture?
premises: Knowledge comes from scripture.
Scripture is not to be heard by the uninitiated.
Initiation serves as the necessary consecration for receiving it.
inference: Therefore initiation is required as consecration so that one may properly receive knowledge from scripture.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What result does a candidate attain when appointed by the teacher in any domain?
premises: The teacher may appoint a candidate in any suitable domain.
The candidate attains a fruit suited to his own understanding.
This has been stated earlier regarding the knower.
inference: Therefore placement by the teacher leads each candidate to a result appropriate to his own level of understanding.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: When does initiation become unnecessary for teacher and disciple?
premises: By the Lord's grace a divine fitness may arise.
This fitness may be present in both teacher and disciple.
In that case initiation has no practical use for them.
inference: Therefore when divine fitness is present by the Lord's grace, initiation is not needed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What takes the place of formal initiation when divine fitness is present?
premises: In that exceptional case knowledge itself functions as initiation.
The Traisika explanation supports this view.
Such a person suddenly comes to know the meaning of all scriptures.
inference: Therefore direct knowledge can replace formal initiation and produce immediate scriptural realization.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Who is regarded as the highest-qualified teacher according to the Malini teaching?
premises: The Malini teaching describes a person of innate awareness.
Such a person is the highest-qualified candidate.
A knower of this kind is regarded as a teacher.
inference: Therefore the one with innate awareness and knowledge is regarded as the highest-qualified teacher.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How does the Malini scripture present the teacher's contemplative responsibility?
premises: A teacher may seek benefit for himself or for others.
He should contemplate this teaching accordingly.
The Malini scripture makes the whole matter clear.
inference: Therefore the Malini scripture presents contemplative responsibility as directed toward the benefit of oneself or others.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What different types of fitness among candidates are recognized in the Kairana scripture?
premises: Candidates differ in their fitness.
Some are fit for knowledge, conduct, initiation, or yoga.
The Kairana scripture states this classification.
inference: Therefore the Kairana scripture recognizes multiple graded types of fitness among candidates.
uncertainties: The exact form of the scripture name rendered as kairana is uncertain.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What qualities define the teacher who is declared fit to guide others?
premises: The teacher must have the marks previously described.
He must be skilled in action, yoga, and knowledge.
He must be elevated through successively higher levels.
inference: Therefore the true teacher is one who combines the stated marks, skill in all three domains, and graded attainment.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How should a qualified teacher proceed before performing the rite of initiation?
premises: The teacher must assess the disciple's purification by the descent of power.
He may examine or question the disciple.
Only then should he perform the initiation rite.
inference: Therefore the teacher should verify the disciple's readiness before carrying out initiation.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What should the teacher ask the disciple before beginning the appropriate practice?
premises: The Svacchanda scripture prescribes direct questioning of the disciple.
The teacher should ask what fruit the disciple seeks.
The teacher begins the means suited to that desired fruit.
inference: Therefore the teacher must tailor the practice to the fruit the disciple explicitly desires.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How do shared ritual elements produce different results for different candidates?
premises: Differences in inclination lead to attainment of different goals.
Mantra impels the attainment of those goals.
Mantra, seal, path, and substances are commonly used in the offering.
inference: Therefore common ritual elements can yield different results because they are shaped by differing inclinations and mantra.
uncertainties: The term adhva may refer to a ritual path or level; rendered generally as path.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How does difference of inclination affect the fruits attained by disciples and teachers?
premises: Inclinations differ among disciples and teachers.
Because of this, the fruits they attain differ.
The Shaiva practitioner is classified into two types, including one who abandons worldly life.
inference: Therefore differing inclinations produce different fruits and support a twofold classification of practitioners.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What further distinctions are made among practitioners who remain in the world and those who seek liberation?
premises: One practitioner follows worldly duty, desires fruit, abides in good, and avoids evil.
The seeker of liberation is also divided into types.
One type of liberation-seeker is seedless and free from pledges and related observances.
inference: Therefore practitioners are further distinguished by worldly orientation and by the seedless form of the liberation-seeker.
uncertainties: The contrast implied by dvidha for the mumukṣu is only partly stated in this verse.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Which kind of candidate receives the seeded initiation in the teaching of Shiva?
premises: Some candidates are like children, fools, the old, women, enjoyers, or the sick.
Such a candidate is classed as the other type.
For this type the teaching of Shiva declares a seeded initiation.
inference: The seeded initiation is prescribed for candidates who are not fit for the higher, seedless path.
uncertainties: The compound bālabāliśavṛddhastrībhogabhugvyādhitādikaḥ may be read as a list of examples rather than a strict class definition.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What kind of initiation must those who endure the pairs of opposites observe?
premises: Some candidates are able to endure the pairs of opposites.
For them a seeded initiation consisting of pledges confers grace.
They must also observe the special pledges.
inference: Candidates who endure opposites receive a seeded, pledge-based initiation and are bound to keep its special pledges.
uncertainties: vidvaddvandva may refer to learned endurance of opposites or more generally to those who can bear dualities.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How should the actions of a desireless seeker of liberation be treated in initiation?
premises: A desireless seeker of liberation aims only at release.
Past and future actions can be contemplated as non-existent.
Actions already begun must still run their course.
inference: For a desireless seeker, initiation should dissolve past and future karma but not the karma already begun.
uncertainties: śādhayet could be read as 'should purify' or 'should bring to effect'; the context favors not effecting or not removing prārabdha.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How does initiation function for a practitioner who seeks power?
premises: A practitioner may seek power rather than liberation alone.
For such a practitioner purification is performed accordingly.
This initiation belongs to Shiva-duty and removes worldly duty.
inference: The initiation for a power-seeking practitioner purifies in a way that shifts the candidate from worldly duty to Shiva-duty.
uncertainties: itthameva may refer back to the method of verse 27 or indicate a parallel but distinct procedure.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What does the worldly-duty initiation purify and what does it omit?
premises: Some candidates remain within worldly duty.
Their initiation purifies only unrighteous actions.
This initiation does not include mantra worship.
inference: The worldly-duty initiation is limited: it removes unrighteousness but leaves auspicious worldly acts and lacks mantra worship.
uncertainties: The exact ritual scope of mantrārādhanavarjitā is not specified in this verse.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What happens to this initiate after the body shaped by begun karma falls away?
premises: The initiated person still has karma already begun.
When that body breaks, the person enjoys powers such as aṇimā.
After that enjoyment the person goes to a level where they are joined, in sakala or a limited state.
inference: The initiate passes through enjoyment of powers after death and then proceeds to a further level of conjunction.
uncertainties: The exact contrast between sakale and akale in this compound is compressed and may admit more than one technical reading.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What does seedless initiation accomplish for the ripe candidate?
premises: Seedless initiation addresses the bond of pledge-conduct.
Initiation alone can bring liberation in this case.
Constant devotion to god and guru supports that liberation.
inference: In seedless initiation, purification of the pledge-bond leads to liberation through initiation itself together with steady devotion.
uncertainties: The verse leaves open whether devotion is a separate cause or the mode in which initiation becomes effective.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is the seedless initiation said to give immediate liberation?
premises: The seedless initiation is called immediate-liberation-giving.
It severs the three bonds of past, future, and begun karma.
Removing those three bonds removes the basis for continued bondage.
inference: Seedless initiation gives immediate liberation because it cuts all three temporal bonds at once.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What different outcomes follow body abandonment after seedless and seeded initiation?
premises: A purified person may abandon the body at the end of initiation.
In the seedless case the supreme state is attained.
In the seeded case the absence of karma creates a failure or complication.
inference: Seedless initiation can culminate in the supreme state at death, while seeded initiation does not produce the same immediate completion.
uncertainties: vipadyate is terse here; it may mean the expected result fails, or that the person meets an adverse outcome.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What must the initiated person and the guru do after seeded initiation is chosen?
premises: The seeded initiate remains bound to pledge-conduct.
That bond must be guarded continually.
The guru must personally ask, understand, and examine before proceeding.
inference: Seeded initiation requires ongoing pledge observance by the disciple and careful personal assessment by the guru.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How should the guru approach initiation for someone who has received the descent of grace?
premises: The guru wishes to perform a suitable initiation.
The candidate's disposition must match that initiation.
A person who has received the descent of grace comes forward for initiation.
inference: The guru must fit the initiation to the candidate's disposition and must not treat a recipient of grace with disregard.
uncertainties: The sentence continues into verse 36, so the prohibition is completed there.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How must the guru treat a poor person who has received the descent of grace?
premises: Shambhu's command forbids disrespect toward one who has received grace.
A poor person may be unable to pay for initiation.
The guru may use his own wealth to perform the initiation.
inference: The guru must not refuse or belittle a poor recipient of grace and should, if needed, initiate them at his own expense.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What may a disciple offer when seeking initiation despite poverty?
premises: A disciple may lack ordinary wealth for initiation.
The disciple may beg for initiation even with durva grass and water.
Any wealth obtained by begging or owned personally should first be given to the guru.
inference: Even minimal or begged offerings are acceptable for initiation if they are first offered to the guru.
uncertainties: The ritual role of durva grass and water is stated minimally here, without further detail.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What makes an offering fit for initiation and what first qualifies a guru?
premises: Wealth given to the guru becomes purified and fit for offering.
The guru's qualification must be established first.
The essential qualification is entry into the freedom of Shiva-state.
inference: A proper offering is purified by being given to the guru, and the true guru is defined first by living entry into Shiva's freedom.
uncertainties: The compound śivatāpattisvātantryāveśa is dense and may emphasize attainment, freedom, or indwelling as aspects of one state.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Who is truly fit to act as guru in initiation?
premises: Only one who has entered the freedom of Shiva-state is truly a guru.
Such a person is capable of performing initiation.
Many means for entering that Shiva-state have already been shown.
inference: The capacity to initiate depends on the guru's real entry into Shiva-state, which can be reached by many methods.
uncertainties: The verse alludes to previously taught methods without naming them.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How can external ritual acts lead to the state of Shiva?
premises: There is a gradual path that takes an external form.
It uses practices such as bathing, placement, and worship.
Within these many acts, Shiva-state can be established in the heart.
inference: External ritual practice can serve as a gradual means for inwardly establishing the state of Shiva.
uncertainties: The verse continues into verse 41, so the result of establishing Shiva-state is completed there.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What follows when Shiva-state is firmly established in the heart?
premises: A clear-minded practitioner can firmly establish Shiva-state within.
By doing so the practitioner attains Shiva-being.
One who has become Shiva acts according to that realized freedom.
inference: Firm inward establishment of Shiva-state leads to Shiva-being and to action grounded in that realization.
uncertainties: The freedom to do whatever one wishes is framed by the attained Shiva-state, not by ordinary desire.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What makes an external means effective for liberation in the teacher-disciple relation?
premises: An external means by itself is not the cause of liberation.
Liberation requires identification with Shiva.
Teacher and disciple must share the firm recognition 'this is Shiva; I am Shiva.'
inference: External practice gives liberation only when it is grounded in a firm Shiva-identification shared by teacher and disciple.
uncertainties: The compound at the end is compressed; the exact distribution of the recognition between teacher and disciple is interpretive.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why must inner realization and outer practice be joined for liberation?
premises: Firm identification functions through a cause-and-possessor relation between teacher and disciple.
That firm identification is what liberates.
External practice without inner realization fails, and inner realization without external form is also incomplete.
inference: Liberation requires the union of inner realization and outer practice, grounded in firm shared identification.
uncertainties: The phrase hetutadvattayā is philosophically compressed and may refer to the guru as cause and the disciple as recipient.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What scriptural principle supports the union of knowledge and action?
premises: Success comes through knowledge and action together.
This paired principle is clearly manifested.
The revered Brahmayamala is cited as authority for this teaching.
inference: The union of knowledge and action is established by scriptural authority, not merely by inference.
uncertainties: The quoted fragment beginning with deva is too brief to recover the full original sentence.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why does the wise person perform bathing and related observances?
premises: The revered Ananda scripture is cited on this point.
For the wise person there is no real impurity.
Bathing and wearing good clothes produce contentment.
inference: For the wise, ritual bathing is not for removing impurity but for generating contentment and fitness.
uncertainties: suvastratvaṃ may refer broadly to clean or proper dress rather than specifically fine garments.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How does true purity arise for those who perform bathing?
premises: Bathing involves the familiar sequence of purifying body and related measures.
Through that sequence one can enter inwardly without strain.
Such inward entry produces purity for those who bathe.
inference: Ritual bathing yields real purity when its outer sequence leads to effortless inward entry.
uncertainties: mātṛ in this compound is technical and may refer to measures, principles, or limiting factors; the gloss keeps it general.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the inner meaning of bathing in relation to the God of Gods?
premises: Bathing is connected with the eight forms of the God of Gods.
Mantra can kindle an inner burning of impurity.
Immersion in that inner burning constitutes the deeper bath.
inference: The true bath is inward immersion in mantra-kindled purification, grounded in the deity's eightfold form.
uncertainties: The verse assumes knowledge of the eight forms without listing them.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is the earthly bath performed and what effect does it have?
premises: The practitioner is centered in the heart of the chosen mantra.
The rite involves going and returning three steps within the measure of cow dust.
This earthly bath gives steadiness.
inference: The earthly bath is a mantra-centered ritual movement that produces steadiness.
uncertainties: gorajas is a traditional measure; the exact practical distance may vary by ritual convention.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How should the practitioner wash the body with consecrated waters?
premises: Impurity is removed using clay consecrated by the weapon mantra.
Waters are consecrated by the five-limb mantras.
The body is washed in order from head to feet.
inference: After removing impurity with consecrated clay, the practitioner should sequentially wash the body from head to feet with waters empowered by the five-limb mantras.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What should the practitioner do during and after immersion in water?

question: Whom should the practitioner satisfy with water and the Malini mantra?
premises: The sun is satisfied with water using the Malini mantra.

Gods, ancestors, sages, yakshas, demons, and other elemental beings are also satisfied.
inference: By offering water with the Malini mantra to the sun, the satisfier of all, the practitioner also satisfies gods, ancestors, sages, yakshas, demons, and other elemental beings.

question: What principle underlies the satisfaction of all beings and what follows it?
premises: The vital breath, whose nature is power, satisfies all beings.
That same power is identified with the sun.
After this, one recites the single supreme mantra by the previously taught method of utterance.
inference: Because the vital breath as power is the sun, satisfying all through it is effective, and the practitioner then recites the single supreme mantra as previously taught.

question: What completes the water bath and what begins the fire bath?
premises: Water bathing is regarded as complete through awareness of becoming one with that reality.
Ash arisen from fire is used for the next form of bathing.

premises: Hands and feet are washed with water alone after the ash application.
Sipping water, satisfaction offerings, and recitation follow.
This sequence constitutes the ash bath.
inference: The ash bath is completed by washing, sipping, satisfaction, and recitation, and it is classified as the fiery bath.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is the wind bath performed using a gentle breeze and mantra?
premises: A refreshing wind, not excessive and like dust raised by cows, is present.
The practitioner utters the mantra.
The practitioner may move back and forth in that wind.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What purity arises from contemplating the stainless sky with mantra?
premises: The practitioner sits with a one-pointed gaze on the stainless, pervasive sky.
The practitioner remembers the mantra while doing so.
The verse rhetorically asks what purity could surpass this.
inference: Contemplation of the stainless sky with one-pointed gaze and mantra remembrance yields a supreme purity beyond comparison.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What alternative practice counts as the sky bath using falling water?
premises: Water falls from the stainless sky.
That falling water touches the body.
The practitioner is joined with mantra recitation during this contact.

question: What limitless fitness arises from bathing in the lights with Shiva-awareness?
premises: The practitioner contemplates moon, sun, and fire lights with the state of Shiva.
Immersion and purification occur through this contemplation and the Malini.
The verse rhetorically denies any limit to the practitioner's fitness.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How does the self function as the ultimate bath beyond ritual?
premises: The self alone is the supreme lord.
The self is a great pool beyond ritual observance.
The universe is immersed in that self and abides there.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How should the eight baths be ranked and completed with mantra?
premises: There is a group of eight baths.

premises: The eight baths are practiced in order.

inference: The sage devoted to the eight baths attains, in order, firmness, nourishment, burning of impurity, power, pervasion, purification, abiding, and finally non-difference.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the essential nature of the eight forms and how do they give fruit?
premises: The eight forms are gracious in nature.
They are essentially forms of Shiva.
Meditation through one's own form and Shiva's form makes them give their respective fruits.
inference: The eight gracious forms, being Shiva in essence, grant their respective fruits when meditated upon through one's own form and Shiva's form.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How does applying this method in worship yield the fruits of the elements?
premises: The method is applied in worship.
It includes the application beginning with the bulb and support.

question: How do mantras correspond to the levels in yogic application?
premises: In the movement of yoga, mantras align with the levels where they are applied.
On earth they are earthly and in water they are watery.
This correspondence continues up to Shiva, where they are of Shiva's nature.
inference: In yogic application, mantras take on the character of each level, from earth up to Shiva, where they become wholly of Shiva's nature.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

premises: The revered Nirmaryada scripture explains this matter well.
Earth and the other elements have a special form.
That special form is approved by heroic practitioners.

premises: Battle dust is treated as the heroic water.

question: What completes the heroic eightfold set used in bathing and worship?
premises: The self is included in the heroic set.
That self is well established after all affliction of conceptual thought has been shaken off.
This eightfold set is to be honored in bathing, worship, and related rites by heroic practitioners.
inference: The heroic eightfold set culminates in the self, free of all conceptual affliction, and this set is to be honored by heroes in bathing and worship.

premises: Worship is performed in the middle of the mantra circle.

premises: The rite includes satisfaction of the deity.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

premises: In wine bathing the best practitioner seeking liberation becomes kevalī.

The pīṭha-place is always fit for worship.

inference: The seat beyond maya is the previously stated form of Brahma and others, free of maya collyrium.
uncertainties: āsanaṃ may mean support or seat.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is placed above Rudra and what is it called in scriptures?
premises: Above Rudra place Ishvara god.
Above that place Sadasiva.
He is called Mahapreta in scriptures.
inference: The ascent places Ishvara above Rudra and Sadasiva above Ishvara, called Mahapreta.
uncertainties: nyasyetsa may mean he should place or he is placed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is Mahapreta absorbed and not going downward?
premises: Mahapreta pervades all tattvas.
From awakening and excellent going he is absorbed.
He would not go downward.
inference: Mahapreta is absorbed through awakening and excellent going, not descending.
uncertainties: prabodhataḥ may mean from instruction rather than awakening.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Where do all lords of vidya and avidya ultimately resort?
premises: All lords of vidya and avidya have gone higher and higher.
Having become Sadasiva, they then resort to supreme Shiva.
inference: The lords of vidya and avidya ascend to Sadasiva and then to supreme Shiva.
uncertainties: uttarottaratāṃ may mean successive superiority.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is Sadasiva described as thin and preta?
premises: Therefore Sadasiva is always upward-gazing luminous self.
He is thin due to measurability and weakness.
He is preta from loud laughter and such.
inference: Sadasiva's thinness and preta status follow from measurability, weakness, and loud laughter.
uncertainties: The causal phrase is compressed and possibly corrupt.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What should one remember rising from the navel?
premises: From him, risen from the navel, exited through three crown openings.
Remember sound-end self, Śakti-pervading, mind-bright.
inference: The verse instructs remembering the sound-end self pervaded by Śakti and bright in mind.
uncertainties: Parsing of nādāntātma.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the thirty-seven-self seat?
premises: Three spokes, twelve-ended, there also beyond-mind three.
Of lotuses white, this is the thirty-seven-self seat.
inference: The verse identifies a white lotus seat of thirty-seven selves with beyond-mind triad.
uncertainties: Parsing of saptatriṃśadātmedamāsanam.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How are all principles remembered here?
premises: Here all principles with distinction-breath.
From that, distinct as seat, indeed object of consciousness is remembered.
inference: All principles are remembered as distinct seat and object of consciousness.
uncertainties: Parsing of yattataḥ.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What happens to these principles in supreme Bhairava?
premises: These very principles are dissolved in supreme Bhairava.
Then by identity they are created in distinction-deva-worship-joining.
inference: The principles dissolve in supreme Bhairava and are recreated in worship-joining.
uncertainties: Parsing of bhidevārcyatvayojane.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What do these principles attain?
premises: Having Śrī Bhairava knowledge-unity gain freedom, these very principles attain worshipper-hood enough.
inference: The principles attain worshipper-hood through Śrī Bhairava knowledge-unity freedom.
uncertainties: Parsing of śrīmadbhairavabodhaikyalābhasvātantryavanti.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the worshipper and worshipped?
premises: The worshipper is supreme-principle self.
The worshipped principle is supreme-inferior.
Because created, inferior principle-net is seat-state foundation.
inference: Worshipper is supreme self; worshipped principle ranges from supreme to inferior created net.
uncertainties: Parsing of tattvajālamāsanatāspadam.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What are the scriptural endpoints?
premises: Ending at vidyā-kalā in Siddhānta.
Ending at Sadāśiva in left-right scriptures.
Ending at Samanā in Mata Yāmala.
inference: Different scriptures have different endpoints: vidyā-kalā, Sadāśiva, or Samanā.
uncertainties: Meaning of samanā.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the supreme seat here?
premises: Ending at unmanā, here called this supreme seat.
Having worshipped the seat, the worshipped guru line is as Bhāvin.
inference: The supreme seat ends at unmanā; after worship, the guru line is worshipped as Bhāvin.
uncertainties: Parsing of unmanāntamihākhyātamityetatparamāsanam.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is placed in that seat?
premises: In that seat, formerly embodied, with half-syllable, two.
Place as pervader-ness, thus said in Siddha Yogīśvarī Mata.
inference: In that seat one places the two embodied half-syllable forms as pervader-ness.
uncertainties: Parsing of nyasyedvyāptṛtayetyuktaṃ.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How should Sadāśiva be worshipped?
premises: Worship Sadāśiva, great preta image, with half-syllable.
As supreme, supreme above, with incense, flowers, etc., thus.
inference: Sadāśiva is worshipped as supreme above with incense, flowers, and other offerings.
uncertainties: Meaning of mahāpretaṃ.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is the second image imagined?
premises: Imagine the vidyā-image, then self-named, second.
In middle Bhairava true-being; on right Rati-crest.
inference: The second image is imagined with Bhairava true-being in the middle and Rati-crest on the right.
uncertainties: Parsing of vidyāmūrtimathātmākhyāṃ.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How are the nine-self and triad arranged?
premises: Nine-self; on left that devī-like Bhairava triad.
In middle supreme full-moon image; on right again.
inference: The arrangement places the triad on the left, supreme full-moon image in the middle, and again on the right.
uncertainties: Parsing of vāmatastaddevīvadbhairavatrayam.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How are the left and right goddess forms distinguished?
premises: The higher-lower form is red and slightly pointed.
The lower form is terrifying and black-tawny.
The left horn holds the terrifying form.
inference: The verse distinguishes two goddess forms by color, shape, and placement.
uncertainties: Exact syntactic relation of na bhīṣaṇām is compressed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is the imagined form to be contemplated after placement?
premises: Placement is done in the body as before, twofold and sixfold.
Then one should imagine the fitting imagined form of these.
The form is contemplated after placement.
inference: The verse prescribes contemplation of a fitting imagined form following bodily placement.
uncertainties: vapurāsāṃ is a fused genitive compound.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What forms are assigned according to action difference?
premises: Forms are assigned according to action difference.
They have two, four, or six arms and so on.
They bear skull, trident, club, boon, fear, pot, and so on.
inference: The verse lists multi-armed forms and their implements according to action difference.
uncertainties: The exact list of implements is compressed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why are the goddesses imagined with variegated placement?
premises: One imagines because of variegated left-right placement.
In reality these goddesses are universal forms.
They are consciousness-natured.
inference: The variegated placement is imagined because the goddesses are in reality universal consciousness-natured forms.
uncertainties: The fused verb ending is embedded in the first token.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the essence of the goddesses and what follows?
premises: Their essence is unlimited consciousness alone.
They may be for liberation.
Then all limbs, faces, and so on, world-guardians, weapons, last.
inference: The goddesses are unlimited consciousness-essence for liberation, followed by limbs, faces, guardians, weapons, and last items.
uncertainties: The exact relation of sarvaṃ to the following compound is compressed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What triad becomes worshipful in the middle?
premises: In the middle the goddess-named worshipful triad becomes.
It is worshiped.
Then from the middle-seated consciousness-mass and eternal unity.
inference: The middle holds a worshipful goddess triad, worshiped from the seated consciousness-mass and eternal unity.
uncertainties: The ablative chain is syntactically compressed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the spark-natured emanation worshiped separately?
premises: Limbs and so on are emanated and worshipful.
They are spark-natured and separate.
The goddess going in the middle is indeed she, true-being-formed.
inference: The spark-natured emanated limbs are worshiped separately, while the middle goddess is true-being-formed.
uncertainties: The relation between pṛthak and madhyagā is compressed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is the time-drawing goddess praised?
premises: The time-drawing goddess is fierce, peaceful, and mixed everywhere.
In the siddha tantra she is with one syllable.
The supreme goddess is thus praised.
inference: The time-drawing goddess is praised as fierce, peaceful, and mixed, with one syllable in the siddha tantra.
uncertainties: saikārṇā may modify the goddess or the tantra context.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What should be placed in the middle?
premises: The supreme mother goddess Mālinī is middle-risen.
In the middle one should place sun-radiance.
It is all-letters-composed and supreme.
inference: The middle-risen supreme mother goddess Mālinī is associated with placing all-letters-composed supreme sun-radiance in the middle.
uncertainties: The exact object of nyasyet is compressed with sūryaruciṃ.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What emerges and is worshiped from her crest?
premises: At her crest-tip is indeed the one-syllabled.
Her limbs and so on are thus.
Then the universe emerged and is worshiped in south and north.
inference: From her crest the one-syllabled and her limbs are set, then the universe emerges and is worshiped in both directions.
uncertainties: The fused tvaikārṇāṃ and tasyāścāṅgādikaṃ are compressed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is worship to be performed once in the middle?
premises: It may indeed be worshiped by that.
Once in the middle one should worship.
It is said in the Shridevi tantra sacrifice named Damara.
inference: The verse directs worship once in the middle, as stated in the Shridevi tantra sacrifice named Damara.
uncertainties: The exact antecedent of tena is compressed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Where does the time-drawing goddess draw time?
premises: At the nose-tip is threefold time.
The time-drawing goddess is always mouth-situated.
Calculating breath and inbreath, she draws in the heart.
inference: The time-drawing goddess, always situated in the mouth and calculating breath, draws threefold time in the heart.
uncertainties: The exact relation of nāsāgre to kālaṃ is compressed.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How do the phases of breath relate to the seizing of time?
premises: With inhalations and retentions the power holds and seizes time.
With exhalation it completely seizes all time.
Risen with exhalation, it acts in an instant.
inference: The breath phases progressively master time, culminating in instantaneous total seizure through exhalation.
uncertainties: The subject of grasate/saṃgrasate is carried from the preceding context (the power).

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Which power is to be worshipped and what does it accomplish?
premises: The supreme will-power, named as the awakener of the three powers, is to be worshipped.
It draws in everything.
Its action shatters the support of time.
inference: Worship of the supreme will-power, which awakens the three powers, results in the drawing in of all and the collapse of time's foundation.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How do the powers of seeing, action, and will manifest in different subjects?
premises: The powers of seeing, action, and will have been spoken of, O Shiva.
In the gross and subtle cutting of the knowable, in order, they operate.
They become the sakala and pralayākala subjects respectively.
inference: The three powers, operating at gross and subtle levels of knowable-division, correspond to the sakala and pralayākala states.
uncertainties: The exact mapping of gross/subtle to sakala/pralayākala is compressed in the verse.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What states arise when the powers are asleep or awakened in purity?
premises: When pure but asleep, the powers become the state of the knowledge-limited subject.
When awakened, they know some divided knowables.
In that awakened state they are called mantras.
inference: The same pure powers yield the vijñānākala state when asleep and the mantra level when awakened to partial knowledge.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How do higher lordly subjects arise as the knowable becomes fully or partly divided?
premises: When the entire knowable is divided, the lords of mantras and great lords arise.
When the knowable is both divided and undivided, the path up to Sadāśiva arises.
This culminates in the supreme Lord.
inference: Degrees of division in the knowable correspond to ascending levels from mantreśas to Sadāśiva and the supreme Lord.
uncertainties: The compound suśivānto@dhvoditaḥ is read as the path arisen up to Sadāśiva.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How do the powers transform as difference expands and then dissolves?
premises: As the expansion of difference dissolves, the powers gradually come to expansion.
Mutually mixed, they become the triad of tvaras.
When difference has dissolved, they move beyond that triad.
inference: The powers pass from differentiated expansion to a mutually mixed triad and then to a state where difference is dissolved.
uncertainties: tvarātrayaṃ refers to the triad of tvaras in the Trika system; kept as a technical term in sense.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What forms the seat of worship and why do the powers assume it?
premises: The triad of lotuses together with unmanā functions as the seat.
The powers assume this seat.
They do so from a desire to cut off their mutual difference.
inference: The lotus triad and unmanā serve as the ritual seat because the powers seek to transcend their mutual differentiation.
uncertainties: The verse is syntactically compressed; the causal link is inferred from the instrumental.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why do the divisions of power and its possessor become objects of worship?
premises: The divisions of power, its possessor, and so on come to be worshipped.
This begins from the first point where difference dissolves.
From that point each bears its own proper form.
inference: These divisions become worshippable because, from the threshold of dissolving difference, each manifests its own true form.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is the threefoldness of these powers clearly perceived?
premises: The powers bear a threefold structure.
Their threefoldness is clearly perceived.
This clarity arises from possible impurity of the knowable and mutual mixture.
inference: The triadic distinction becomes evident because of the knowable's potential impurity and the powers' mutual intermixture.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is the supreme consciousness called Kālakarṣiṇī rather than threefold?
premises: Before this level the threefold state does not appear in the same clear way.
This consciousness is ready to devour the cutting of mutual difference.
Its essence is freedom alone, and so it is called Kālakarṣiṇī.
inference: Because it transcends triadic division by consuming difference and rests in pure freedom, consciousness is named Kālakarṣiṇī.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is the same consciousness also called Saṃkarṣiṇī among the Mothers?
premises: She draws time back into herself.
She expels time outward here.
Among these Mothers this is her true mode of being, so she is called Saṃkarṣiṇī.
inference: Her dual act of drawing in and projecting out time establishes her identity as Saṃkarṣiṇī among the Mothers.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the true nature and supreme reality of the Mothers and powers?
premises: True nature, being, and attainment are measured in relation to the Mothers.
This applies to the world-generating powers.
Their supreme reality is nothing but freedom.
inference: The ontological status of the Mothers and powers is grounded in their supreme reality, which is sheer autonomy.
uncertainties: meyo@nayā is read as 'by this measure/criterion' in a compressed doctrinal sense.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is the reality of willing, knowing, and acting worthy of worship?
premises: The worshippable reality consists of willing, knowing, and acting.
It is unlimited.
All directions of limitation are gathered within it.
inference: Because it is unbounded and contains all possible limitations, the triad of willing, knowing, and acting is supremely worshippable.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why does worshippability require a conceptual state that gathers many attributes?
premises: The non-conceptual does not attain worshippability here.
A single conceptual construction does not suffice where many attributes are present.
Therefore one attribute must gather in that many attributes.
inference: Worshippability arises not in bare non-conceptuality but in a unifying conceptual focus that comprehends many attributes.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the principle of supreme Bhairava worship taught in the Ḍāmara?
premises: That which draws in all attributes is established there as supreme.
All others stand in a lower position.
This is the principle of supreme Bhairava worship in the great rite of the revered Ḍāmara.
inference: Supreme worship centers on the unifying principle that comprehends all attributes, as taught in the Ḍāmara's great rite.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How should worship be performed in the external rite according to Śambhu's teaching?
premises: The glorious Śambhu himself, well pleased, taught this to me.
In the external rite, worship is to be performed.
It should be done in the triad of lotuses as well.
inference: Following Śambhu's direct teaching, external worship must be carried out upon the triad of lotuses.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is the retinue arranged in the directions according to the instructors' teaching?
premises: The retinue multitude is arranged ending with the weapon mantra.
This is stated in the teaching of the instructors.
The fivefold group of vidyā-limbs is placed in the directions of fire, Īśa, the demons, Vāyu, and the intermediate quarters.
inference: The instructors prescribe a directional installation of the retinue culminating in the weapon mantra and the five vidyā-limbs.
uncertainties: The exact mapping of the five directions is compressed; read as the specified quarters including intermediate ones.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Where are the limbs of Śakti and Śiva and the weapon and Locana mantras placed?
premises: The limbs of Śakti and the limbs of Śiva are placed likewise here.
Again in the pair, the weapon mantra should be placed in the four directions.
In the middle one should place the mantra called Locana.
inference: The ritual installation distributes Śakti and Śiva limbs, places the weapon mantra to the four directions, and centers Locana.
uncertainties: The phrase 'again in the pair' is terse and may refer to a paired ritual context from the surrounding passage.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How are the mantra groups arranged on the petals and in further sets?
premises: On the eight petals a pair of octads beginning with Aghorā is placed according to its own tradition.
Likewise groups of twelve, six, and four are used.
These are arranged mixed, two by two.
inference: The rite layers octads, then sets of twelve, six, and four, distributing them in paired combinations according to tradition.
uncertainties: svayāmalam is read as 'according to its own tradition/Āmala source'.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How should the enclosing worship and the world guardians be arranged?
premises: Worship should be performed in every way as a doubled enclosure.
Then the world guardians should be worshipped.
They are placed with their weapons in their own ten directions in order.
inference: The rite proceeds by doubled concentric worship followed by sequential installation of the world guardians in all ten directions.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: From what inner stance should the practitioner satisfy the host of deities?
premises: The practitioner abides in identity with the goddesses up to the trident.
Standing in that state, he offers the universe.
By this he should satisfy the host of deities.
inference: Satisfaction of the deities is accomplished by offering the universe while identified with the goddess-powers of the trident.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How should mantra recitation be performed after the offering?
premises: After that one should perform recitation.
Each mantra is recited ten times.
Because each is threefold in nature and yet non-different, this applies in all respects.
inference: Recitation proceeds mantra by mantra, ten times each, grounded in the mantras' simultaneous threefoldness and unity.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is the mantra circle visualized and used for inner oblation?
premises: The mantra circle is remembered like fire in the navel, heart, throat, palate, and upper center.
There the universe is present.
Burning it, one should accomplish the oblation.
inference: Internal recitation culminates in a fiery visualization of the mantra circle that consumes the universe as an inner offering.
uncertainties: jvahvan is read as a participial form related to burning (√jval).

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Where should the teacher first apply the path of initiation when performing the rite?
premises: When the act of initiation is to be performed, the teacher chooses a path.
Desiring to perform initiation, he begins in the body.
At first he should primarily apply that path there.
inference: The initiation path selected by the teacher is first and foremost applied within the disciple's body.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What result comes from meditating on the trident up to the twelve-end-point?
premises: One remembers the trident extending from the root to the twelve-end-point.
One reaches the tip of the goddess-circle and abandons sequential progression.
This meditation produces the state of moving in space.
inference: By meditating on the trident to the twelve-end-point and transcending sequence, the practitioner attains khecaratā.
uncertainties: The exact referent of dvādaśānta in this ritual context is assumed from standard Tantric usage.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Why is this power called khecarī in this context?
premises: Khecarī fills the path from the root-support to the top of the space at the end of the twelve.
She is associated with moving and abiding in space.
She is associated with feeding on the nectar of space.
inference: The name khecarī is explained by her pervasion of the inner space and her movement, abiding, and nourishment in that space.
uncertainties: dviṣaṭka is taken as referring to the twelvefold endpoint in line with the previous verse.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How are the Śākta and Āṇava tridents positioned relative to the Śāmbhava trident?
premises: The Śāmbhava trident is the reference point.
The Śākta trident is reduced by four finger-widths from it.
The Āṇava trident is reduced by four finger-widths from the Śākta.
inference: A triad of tridents is established in descending measure from Śāmbhava to Śākta to Āṇava.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What powers belong to one who has offered the self to the goddess-circles on the three tridents?
premises: The practitioner offers the self to the successive goddess-circles on the triad of tridents.
The verse frames the result as a series of rhetorical questions.
Birth, knowledge, and action are all included in the scope of the result.
inference: Such a practitioner is presented as having unrestricted power in becoming, knowing, and doing.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How may each goddess or mantra be worshipped in the lotus?
premises: The worship may focus on each single goddess or each single mantra.
The locus of worship is a lotus.
The form of worship varies by paired-union, limbs, faces, and being or non-being.
inference: The rite allows detailed alternative configurations for worshipping each goddess or mantra in the lotus.
uncertainties: yāmalaikyāṅgavaktrādisadasattāvikalpataḥ is compressed and may admit more than one ritual unpacking.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: When should the external rite be performed in relation to inner transformation?
premises: One's own consciousness is to be made Śiva from the level of breath up to the level of space.
This inner transformation is accomplished through worship-yoga.
The external rite follows that inner preparation.
inference: The external ritual procedure should be performed only after one's consciousness has been inwardly transformed into Śiva.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What role does internal worship play when external worship is treated as primary?
premises: External worship may be pursued for powers and similar aims.
Internal worship serves as purification in that case.
Without that inner purification, the worshipper remains a bound soul.
inference: Even when external worship is primary, internal worship is necessary to purify the practitioner.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the purpose of external worship for one indifferent to powers?
premises: Some practitioners are not oriented toward powers.
They still worship the Lord outwardly.
Their outward worship serves ascent into the inner great worship.
inference: For the disinterested practitioner, external worship is fulfilled when it leads to inner great worship.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What is the sequence for using consecrated grain to remove obstacles?
premises: The inner worship is performed first.
Grain and similar materials are consecrated with the weapon-mantra.
The consecrated material is thrown in the directions and then gathered toward the Īśāna direction.
inference: Obstacle removal proceeds by inner worship, mantra consecration, directional dispersal, and retraction toward Īśāna.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: Which purificatory acts are treated as common in the Triśiras doctrine?
premises: The verse lists inspection, sprinkling, striking, nourishing, and covering.
These acts are grouped as saṃskāras.
They are said to be common in the doctrine of Triśiras.
inference: The Triśiras tradition recognizes a shared set of five purificatory acts.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How are the five cow products consecrated and used for sprinkling?
premises: The five cow products are cow urine, cow dung, curd, milk, and ghee.
They are consecrated with the faces ending in the upper one and with the six limbs.
Kuśa-water is used for sprinkling.
inference: The pañcagavya materials are ritually empowered by mantra and applied through sprinkling with kuśa-water.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: How is the pañcagavya prepared and designated in this rite?
premises: The ground is sprinkled and the remainder is kept for the disciple.
The pañcagavya consists of five cow products.
When these are in kuśa-water, that mixture is called pañcagavya.
inference: The rite defines pañcagavya as the five cow products combined in kuśa-water, used for sprinkling and for the disciple.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What kind of impurity does pañcagavya-water remove according to the scripture?
premises: The scripture identifies pañcagavya-water as removing external impurity.
Ordinary impurity must be removed first.
Only after that is the inner impurity addressed.
inference: Pañcagavya-water functions at the level of external purification, preparing the way for inner purification.

speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
question: What means are used to burn away inner impurity after external purification?
premises: Inner impurity requires a non-ordinary means.
